Dīng Mì devised a plan, having [Cáo] Shuǎng inform Heaven’s Son, to issue an Edict to transfer [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng to be Grand Tutor, outside to use the title honor him, inside wishing to have Secretariat Writer memorial affairs first come through himself, to be able to control their lightness or severity. [25] [Cáo] Shuǎng’s younger brothers [Cáo] Xī became Central Manager of the Army, [Cáo] Xuǹ Martial Guard General, [Cáo] Yàn Cavalier Regular Attendant and Attendant to Lectures, the remaining various younger brothers, all as Ranked Marquesses followed in attendance, exiting and entering the restricted doors, in nobility and favor none could surpass them. Nányáng’s Hé Yàn, Dèng Yáng, Lǐ Shèng, Pèi state’s Dīng Mì, Dōngpíng’s Bì Guǐ all had fame, sought advancement at the time, Emperor Míng believed them superficial and pretentious, restrained and dismissed them all. Reaching to [Cáo] Shuǎng controlling the government, then he again advanced and employed them, appointed as belly and heart. [Dèng] Yáng and the rest wished to have [Cáo] Shuǎng establish authority and fame to Heaven’s Under, urged him to attack Shǔ, [Cáo] Shuǎng followed their advice, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng opposed but could not prohibit it. Zhèngshǐ Fifth Year [244], [Cáo] Shuǎng thus went west reaching Cháng’ān, greatly mobilized soldiers of sixty to seventy thousand men, from Luò valley entering. At the time, the transferred transports from Guānzhōng and the Dī and Qiāng could not supply them, of the oxen and horses and mules and donkeys many died, the civilians and Yí wailed and sobbed on the roads. Entered the valley and traveled several hundred lǐ, the rebels took advantage of the mountains to be firm, the troops could not advance. [Cáo] Shuǎng’s Advisor to the Army Yáng Wěi explained the circumstances to [Cáo] Shuǎng, that it was appropriate to urgently return, and if not then they would be defeated. [26] [Dèng] Yáng and [Yáng] Wěi fought in front of [Cáo] Shuǎng, [Yáng] Wěi said: “[Dèng] Yáng and [Lǐ] Shèng will ruin the country’s affairs, they can be beheaded.” [Cáo] Shuǎng was displeased, and so withdrew the army to return. [27]



爽字昭伯，少以宗室謹重，明帝在東宮，甚親愛之。及即位，為散騎侍郎，累遷城門校尉，加散騎常侍，轉武衛將軍，寵待有殊。帝寢疾，乃引爽入臥內，拜大將軍，假節鉞，都督中外諸軍事，錄尚書事，與太尉司馬宣王並受遺詔輔少主。明帝崩，齊王即位，加爽侍中，改封武安侯，邑萬二千戶，賜劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。丁謐畫策，使爽白天子，發詔轉宣王為太傅，外以名號尊之，內欲令尚書奏事，先來由己，得制其輕重也。〔一〕爽弟羲為中領軍，訓武衛將軍，彥散騎常侍侍講，其餘諸弟，皆以列侯侍從，出入禁闥，貴寵莫盛焉。南陽何晏、鄧颺、李勝、沛國丁謐、東平畢軌咸有聲名，進趣於時，明帝以其浮華，皆抑黜之；及爽秉政，乃復進敘，任為腹心。颺等欲令爽立威名於天下，勸使伐蜀，爽從其言，宣王止之不能禁。正始五年，爽乃西至長安，大發卒六七萬人，從駱谷入。是時，關中及氐、羌轉輸不能供，牛馬騾驢多死，民夷號泣道路。入谷行數百里，賊因山為固，兵不得進。爽參軍楊偉為爽陳形勢，宜急還，不然將敗。〔二〕颺與偉爭於爽前，偉曰：「颺、勝將敗國家事，可斬也。」爽不悅，乃引軍還。〔三〕










[25] Wèi shū states: [Cáo] Shuǎng sent his younger brother [Cáo] Xī to make a memorial that said: “Your Servant’s late father [Cáo] Zhēn served Three Courts, in entering filled in as a senior minister, in exiting was a high officer. The Former Emperor because Your Servant was the heir of a close confidant,76 encouraged and selected me, to organize troops in the Restricted Ministries. In advancing without loyal and respectful accumualted conduct, in withdrawing without the integrity of Gāoyáng’s”from the public,“77 The Former Emperor’s sagely body was unwell, though Your Servant rushed and ran, attending to the illness and tasting the medicine, there was no response to the thorough sincerity on the next day, and I the lowly one with the Grand Commandant [Sīmǎ] Yì together received the Legacy Edict, ashamed and afraid, with nowhere to express it. Your Servant has heard that when Yú Shùn ranked the worthy he had Jì and Qì as the first, that when Chéng Tāng commended achievements he had Yī and Lǚ as the head. To carefully select and widely recommend, the good and the bad in their place, this truly is the great principle for assisting the world and expanding the people, the excellent canon for nothing merits and rewarding achievements, from antiquity onward, never having omission. Now Your Servant is empty and ignorant, position crowning the head of Court, looking back to consider the surpassing of sequence, my heart is ashamed and afraid, I dare exhaust my foolish feelings to explain and write the utmost truth. The observed ways of Heaven’s Under are three, called virtue, nobility, and age. [Sīmǎ] Yì originally for high enlightenment and correct uprightness occupied position of highest minister, fame sufficient to calm the masses, righteousness sufficient to lead subordinates, this is first. He embraces the grand strategy, fully civil fully martial, repeatedly established campaign achievements, far and near assign credit, this is second. Across ten thousand lǐ turning his banners, he personally received the Legacy Edict, supporting and shining the Imperial House, the interior and exterior turn to him, this is third. Adding to this his senior age,78 experienced in regulating country and state, familiar with refining Court and government. In discussing virtue then he surpasses Jí Fǔ and Fán Zhòng, in examining achievements then he exceeds Fāng Shū and Shào Hǔ. Altogether in these several, [Sīmǎ] Yì truly has them all. Your Servant carries an empty name but yet resides to his right, the people of Heaven’s Under will say that Your Servant as a clansman meets with selfish favor, knows to advance but does not know to withdraw. Your Majesty is precociously intelligence, capable of understanding capable of categorization,79 if there is examination of Your Servant’s words, Your Servant believes it appropriate for [Sīmǎ] Yì to be Grand Tutor and Marshal-in-Chief, above to make clear Your Majesty’s enlightenment in advancing worthies, in the middle to make prominent [Sīmǎ] Yì’s embodiment of true civil and martial ability, below to allow Your Humble Servant to escape slander and ridicule.” Thereupon the Emperor sent Central Writers Overseer Liú Fàng and Director Sūn Zī to make Edict that said: “In the past Wú Hàn aided Guāng-Wǔ, having the achievement of campaigning and settling the Four Quarters, became Marshal-in-Chief, his name praised to the present. The Grand tutor embodies and treads the correct and upright, achievements cover Within the Seas, the Former Emperor originally beginning to end had wishes to change his position but always not enough time had passed, and therefore it was delayed and not put into effect. Now the General-in-Chief recommends that the Grand Commandant should be Marshal-in-Chief, it already accords with the Former Emperor’s original intentions, and also demonstrates deferrence, advances virtue and esteems accomplishments, and so wishes to make clear the worthy and good, distinguish hierarchy and rank, and comply with seniority and junior. Even the likes of Dàn and Shì treated Lǚ Wàng as exemplar and teacher, attention on craning neck to reside beneath him, how could it surpass this? We extremely commend it. We consider that the Former Emperor assuredly understood that the noble man delights in Heaven and knows its mandates, minute and triffling doubts are not sufficient for concern, should have considered the examples of Bǎi Rén and Péng Wáng, and therefore employed deliberation and hesitation, having intentions that were not fulfilled. This also was the Former Emperor’s heavy respect for a chief minister, the utmost of deep and generous grace and affection. In the past King Chéng established the offices of Protector and Tutor, more recently Hàn Xiǎnzōng appointed Dèng Yǔ as Grand Tutor, all in order to exceptionally esteem the outstanding, to be certain to have honor. Thus appoint the Grand Commandant as Grand Tutor.”



〔一〕　魏書曰：爽使弟羲為表曰：「臣亡父真，奉事三朝，入備冢宰，出為上將。先帝以臣肺腑遺緒，獎飭拔擢，典兵禁省，進無忠恪積累之行，退無羔羊自公之節。先帝聖體不豫，臣雖奔走，侍疾嘗藥，曾無精誠翼日之應，猥與太尉懿俱受遺詔，且慚且懼，靡所厎告。臣聞虞舜序賢，以稷、契為先，成湯褒功，以伊、呂為首，審選博舉，優劣得所，斯誠輔世長民之大經，錄勳報功之令典，自古以來，未之或闕。今臣虛闇，位冠朝首，顧惟越次，中心愧惕，敢竭愚情，陳寫至實。夫天下之達道者三，謂德、爵、齒也。懿本以高明中正，處上司之位，名足鎮眾，義足率下，一也。包懷大略，允文允武，仍立征伐之勳，遐邇歸功，二也。萬里旋旆，親受遺詔，翼亮皇家，內外所向，三也。加之耆艾，紀綱邦國，體練朝政；論德則過於吉甫、樊仲；課功則踰於方叔、召虎：凡此數者，懿實兼之。臣抱空名而處其右，天下之人將謂臣以宗室見私，知進而不知退。陛下岐嶷，克明克類，如有以察臣之言，臣以為宜以懿為太傅、大司馬，上昭陛下進賢之明，中顯懿身文武之實，下使愚臣免於謗誚。」於是帝使中書監劉放令孫資為詔曰：「昔吳漢佐光武，有征定四方之功，為大司馬，名稱于今。太尉體履正直，功蓋海內，先帝本以前後欲更其位者輒不彌久，是以遲遲不施行耳。今大將軍薦太尉宜為大司馬，既合先帝本旨，又放推讓，進德尚勳，乃欲明賢良、辯等列、順長少也。雖旦、奭之屬，宗師呂望，念在引領以處其下，何以過哉！朕甚嘉焉。朕惟先帝固知君子樂天知命，纖芥細疑，不足為忌，當顧柏人彭亡之文，故用低佪，有意未遂耳！斯亦先帝敬重大臣，恩愛深厚之至也。昔成王建保傅之官，近漢顯宗以鄧禹為太傅，皆所以優崇雋乂，必有尊也。其以太尉為太傅。」













[26] Shìyǔ states: [Yáng] Wěi appellation Shìyīng was a Féngyì man. When Emperor Míng was repairing Palace Residences, [Yáng] Wěi remonstrated stating: “Now to build Palace Residences is to chop down the pines and cypresses above the graves of the people, destroy the stele statues and stone pillars, a crime that reaches the deceased, injures the hearts of filial children, it cannot be an example for later generations.”



〔二〕　世語曰：偉字世英，馮翊人。明帝治宮室，偉諫曰：「今作宮室，斬伐生民墓上松柏，毀壞碑獸石柱，辜及亡人，傷孝子心，不可以為後世之法則。」

〔三〕　漢晉春秋曰：司馬宣王謂夏侯玄曰：「春秋責大德重，昔武皇帝再入漢中，幾至大敗，君所知也。今興平路勢至險，蜀已先據；若進不獲戰，退見徼絕，覆軍必矣。將何以任其責！」玄懼，言於爽，引軍退。費禕進兵據三嶺以截爽，爽爭嶮苦戰，僅乃得過。所發牛馬運轉者，死失略盡，羌、胡怨嘆，而關右悉虛耗矣。







Previously, [Cáo] Shuǎng believed [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s years and virtue were both high, always treated him like a father, not daring to act alone. Reaching to when [Hé] Yàn and the rest were advanced and employed, they all together endorsed him, persuading [Cáo] Shuǎng that heavy authority should not be entrusted to others. Thus appointed [Hé] Yàn, [Dèng] Yáng, [Dīng] Mì as Secretariat Writers, [Hé] Yàn managed selections and recommendations, [Bì] Guǐ Director of Retainers Colonel, [Lǐ] Shèng Hénán Intendant, various affairs were rarely ever through [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng therefore claimed illness and avoided [Cáo] Shuǎng. The relevant managers watched the winds, none daring to disobey their wishes. [Hé] Yàn and the rest with Minister of Justice Lú Yù formerly were not at peace, took advantage of [Lú] Yù’s clerk having a minor transgression, with harsh words sent [Lú] Yù to the law,83 having the manager in advance confiscate [Lú] Yù’s seal and ribbon and only afterwards memorializing report. Their creation of power was like this.84 [Cáo] Shuǎng’s drink and food and chariots and clothing imitated the Chariot Carriage,85 Rare treasures from the Secretariat Crafters86 filled his house, wives and concubines filled his Rear Court, and also he privately took the Former Emperor’s Talent Ladies87 of seven to eight women, with officers and clerks and master artisans and drummers and trumpeters and daughters of elite families of thirty-three people, all to be his performers and musicians. He falsely made Edict letters to send Talent Ladies of fifty seven people to Yè Terrace, having the Former Emperor’s beauties88 instruct and train them into performers. He usurped authority to take the Grand Musician’s musical instruments, the Military Arsenal’s restricted weapons. He made an underground room, engraved windows on all four sides, repeatedly with [Hé] Yàn and the rest gathering inside, drinking alcohol and making merry. [Cáo] Xī deeply believed it a great worry, repeatedly remonstrated to stop it, also wrote a book in three fascicle,89 explaining how arrogance and excessiveness attracks disaster and destruction, its statements and intentions extremely cutting, did not dare reprimand [Cáo] Shuǎng, and claimed it was to admonish their various younger brothers in order to show it to [Cáo] Shuǎng. [Cáo] Shuǎng knew it was directed at himself, was extremely displeased. [Cáo] Xī at some times because his remonstrations and explanations were not accepted, shed tears and rose to leave. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng secretly made preparations against them. Ninth Year [248] Winter, Lǐ Shèng was sent out to be Jīng Province Inspector, went to visit [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng claimed his illness was serious, showing an emaciated appearance. [Lǐ] Shèng was not aware, and said it was true. [29]



初，爽以宣王年德並高，恆父事之，不敢專行。及晏等進用，咸共推戴，說爽以權重不宜委之於人。乃以晏、颺、謐為尚書，晏典選舉，軌司隸校尉，勝河南尹，諸事希復由宣王。宣王遂稱疾避爽〔一〕。晏等專政，共分割洛陽、野王典農部桑田數百頃，及壞湯沐地以為產業，承勢竊取官物，因緣求欲州郡。有司望風，莫敢忤旨。晏等與廷尉盧毓素有不平，因毓吏微過，深文致毓法，使主者先收毓印綬，然後奏聞。其作威如此。爽飲食車服，擬於乘輿；尚方珍玩，充牣其家；妻妾盈後庭，又私取先帝才人七八人，及將吏、師工、鼓吹、良家子女三十三人，皆以為伎樂。詐作詔書，發才人五十七人送鄴臺，使先帝婕妤教習為伎。擅取太樂樂器，武庫禁兵。作窟室，綺疏四周，數與晏等會其中，飲酒作樂。羲深以為大憂，數諫止之。又著書三篇，陳驕淫盈溢之致禍敗，辭旨甚切，不敢斥爽，託戒諸弟以示爽。爽知其為己發也，甚不悅。羲或時以諫喻不納，涕泣而起。宣王密為之備。九年冬，李勝出為荊州刺史，往詣宣王。宣王稱疾困篤，示以羸形。勝不能覺，謂之信然。〔二〕










[28] Previously, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng believed [Cáo] Shuǎng was as Wèi’s lungs and bowels and always deferred to palce him ahead, [Cáo] Shuǎng believed [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s fame was heavy, and also withdrew himself to be humble and beneath him. At the time they were praised. When Dīng Mì and Bì Guǐ and the rest were advanced and employed, they repeatedly spoke to [Cáo] Shuǎng stating: “[Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng has great ambitions and has greatly obtained the people’s hearts, you cannot defer to and sincerely entrust him.” Because of this [Cáo] Shuǎng always was suspicious and on guard. Although the appearances of courtesy was preserved, yet in various activities and actions, all were no longer through [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s strenght was unable to contest it, and moreover fearing the disaster, therefore he avoided him.90



〔一〕　初，宣王以爽魏之肺腑，每推先之，爽以宣王名重，亦引身卑下，當時稱焉。丁謐、畢軌等既進用，數言于爽曰：「宣王有大志而甚得民心，不可以推誠委之。」由是爽恆猜防焉。禮貌雖存，而諸所興造，皆不復由宣王。宣王力不能爭，且懼其禍，故避之。













[29] Wèi Mò zhuàn states: [Cáo] Shuǎng and the rest ordered [Lǐ] Shèng to take leave of [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng, and also spy and examine him. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng met [Lǐ] Shèng, [Lǐ] Shèng explained himself as having no other achievements, undeservedly covered in special favor, about to return to his home province, and had visited the doors to take leave, not expecting to be given the favor to be able to be granted an audience. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng had two maids attending at his side, holding his clothes, his clothes fell. He further pointed up at his mouth, saying he was thirsty and requested a drink, the maid advanced porridge, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng held a cup to drink the porridge, the porridge all spilled out to stain his chest. [Lǐ] Shèng pitied this, shedding tears for this, spoke to [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng stating: “Now the Ruler Above is still young, Heaven’s Under depends on Your Enlightened Excellency. However the masses all say Your Enlightened Excellency’s old illness is spreading, how could one have thought your honored body would be like this!” [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng slowly further broadly spoke, just barely keeping his breath continuous, saying: “I am old and deeply ill, my death in mornings or evenings. You are about to be assigned to Bìng Province. Bìng Province is near the Hú, work well at it, I fear we will not meet again, what of it?” [Lǐ] Shèng said: “I am about to return to serve my home province, not Bìng Province.”91 [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng then further acted confused and mistaken, stating: “You will arrive at Bìng Province, work hard and care for yourself!” He mixed and disordered his statements, acting as if inarticulate in speaking. [Lǐ] Shèng further said: “I am serving Jīng Province, not Bìng Province.” [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng then acted as if slightly understanding, and spoke to [Lǐ] Shèng stating: “[I, Sīmǎ] Yì am old, thoughts inarticulate and neglectful, not undestanding your words. Now you return to be your Home Province’s Inspector, flourishing in virtue and strong in intensity, well establish achievements and accomplishments. Now you and I will part, considering myself my spirit is becoming weak, later we certainly will not meet again, therefore I wished to exert myself, to serve as a meager host, for parting for both life and death. Let [my sons] the brothers [Sīmǎ] Shī and [Sīmǎ] Zhāo be joined with you as friends, you cannot abandon one another, to accord with [Sīmǎ] Yì’s trifling heart.” Therefore he shed tears and sobbed. [Lǐ] Shèng also deeply sighed, answered stating: “At once I will follow your instructions, pending orders and mandates.” [Lǐ] Shèng took leave and went out, met with [Cáo] Shuǎng and the rest, saying: “The Grand Tutor’s speech was confused and mistaken, his mouth could not hold his cup, pointing south and calling it north. He also said I would about to serve in Bìng Province, I answered I was about to return to serve in Jīng Province, not Bìng Province. Slowly and gradually speaking with him, he had a time of clarity, and only then understood I was about to return to serve in Jīng Province. Also he wished to set up a host’s send-off. He cannot be abandoned, it is appropriate to wait and care for him.” He further toward [Cáo] Shuǎng and the rest shed tears saying: “The Grand Tutor’s illness cannot be again relieved, it makes one mournful.”



〔二〕　魏末傳曰：爽等令勝辭宣王，并伺察焉。宣王見勝，勝自陳無他功勞，橫蒙特恩，當為本州，詣閤拜辭，不悟加恩，得蒙引見。宣王令兩婢侍邊，持衣，衣落；復上指口，言渴求飲，婢進粥，宣王持盃飲粥，粥皆流出沾胸。勝愍然，為之涕泣，謂宣王曰：「今主上尚幼，天下恃賴明公。然眾情謂明公方舊風疾發，何意尊體乃爾！」宣王徐更寬言，才令氣息相屬，說：「年老沈疾，死在旦夕。君當屈并州，并州近胡，好善為之，恐不復相見，如何！」勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州也。」宣王乃復陽為昏謬，曰：「君方到并州，努力自愛！」錯亂其辭，狀如荒語。勝復曰：「當忝荊州，非并州也。」宣王乃若微悟者，謂勝曰：「懿年老，意荒忽，不解君言。今還為本州刺史，盛德壯烈，好建功勳。今當與君別，自顧氣力轉微，後必不更會，因欲自力，設薄主人，生死共別。令師、昭兄弟結君為友，不可相舍去，副懿區區之心。」因流涕哽咽。勝亦長嘆，答曰：「輒當承教，須待敕命。」勝辭出，與爽等相見，說：「太傅語言錯誤，口不攝杯，指南為北。又云吾當作并州，吾答言當還為荊州，非并州也。徐徐與語，有識人時，乃知當還為荊州耳。又欲設主人祖送。不可舍去，宜須待之。」更向爽等垂淚云：「太傅患不可復濟，令人愴然。」







Tenth Year Standard Moon [249 Jan 31 - Feb 28], the Chariot Carriage held Court at Gāopínglíng, [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers all following. [30] [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng organized divisions of troops and horses, first occupied the Military Arsenal, then set out to garrison the Luò river’s pontoon bridges. The memorial against [Cáo] Shuǎng said: “Your Servant in the past from Liáodōng returned, the Former Emperor had Edict on Your Majesty and the King of Qín with Your Servant to ascend to the Imperial bed, grasped Your Servant’s arm, deeply concerned with later affairs. Your Servant said: ‘The Two Founders also entrusted Your Servant with later affairs. This Your Majesty personally saw, there is nothing to worry or suffer about. Ten thousand to one if there is anything not as you intend, Your Servant will with my death serve your Enlightened Edict.’ The Yellow Gate Director Dǒng Jī and the rest, the Talent Ladies and attendants to the illness, all heard and know of this. Now the General-in-Chief [Cáo] Shuǎng turns back on and abandons the legacy mandate, ruins and disorders state canon, inside then usurps and imitates, outside concentrates authority and power, destroys the various camps, completely seizing the Restricted Troops, the various offices and criticial positions are all filled by his intimates, Inside the Halls and the Residential Guard, the long serving men through successive generations all were also dismissed and excelled, wishing to install new men to cultivate his personal plans, his roots occupy and twist together, his lack of restraint daily grows more extreme. With the exterior already like this, he also appointed the Yellow Gate Zhāng Dāng as supervisor overseer, to control all interactions, watching the Utmost Honored, spying on the Divine Vessels, estranging the Two Palaces, injuring bone and flesh.92 Heaven’s Under is in turmoil, people filled with apprehension and dread, Your Majesty is only filling a seat, how can there be long-term security? This is not the original intention of the Former Emperor’s Edict on Your Majesty and Your Servant to ascend to the Imperial bed. Although Your Servant is decrepit and old, dare I forget the past93 words? In the past Zhào Gāo had extreme intentions, the Qín clan was thus exterminated.94 Lǚ and Huò were early cut off, Hàn’s blessings endured throught the ages.95 This then is a great reflection for Your Majesty, the time for Your Servant to receive command. Grand Commandant Your Servant [Jiǎng] Jì, Secretariat Writers Director Your Servant [Sīmǎ] Fú and others all believe that [Cáo] Shuǎng has a heart without loyalty to lord, his brothers should not manage the troops and the Residential Guard, and memorialized the Yǒngníng Palace.96 The Imperial Dowager Empress ordered Your Servant to by the memorial put it into effect. Your Servant at once ordered the managers and the Yellow Gate Director to dismiss the clerks and troops of [Cáo] Shuǎng, [Cáo] Xī, [Cáo] Xùn, with them to as Marquesses go to their mansions, to not remain to delay the Chariot Carriage. If any dare to delay and remain, then by Military Law handle the affair. Your Servant at once forces through my illness to lead troops to garrison the Luò river pontoon bridge, to watch for the out of the ordinary.” [31]



十年正月，車駕朝高平陵，爽兄弟皆從。〔一〕宣王部勒兵馬，先據武庫，遂出屯洛水浮橋。奏爽曰：「臣昔從遼東還，先帝詔陛下、秦王及臣升御床，把臣臂，深以後事為念。臣言『二祖亦屬臣以後事，（為念）此自陛下所見，無所憂苦；萬一有不如意，臣當以死奉明詔』。黃門令董箕等，才人侍疾者，皆所聞知。今大將軍爽背棄顧命，敗亂國典，內則僭擬，外專威權；破壞諸營，盡據禁兵，群官要職，皆置所親；殿中宿衛，歷世舊人皆復斥出，欲置新人以樹私計；根據槃互，縱恣日甚。外既如此，又以黃門張當為都監，專共交關，看察至尊，侯伺神器，離間二宮，傷害骨肉。天下洶洶，人懷危懼，陛下但為寄坐，豈得久安！此非先帝詔陛下及臣升御床之本意也。臣雖朽邁，敢忘枉言？昔趙高極意，秦氏以滅；呂、霍早斷，漢祚永世。此乃陛下之大鑒，臣受命之時也。太尉臣濟、尚書令臣孚等，皆以爽為有無君之心，兄弟不宜典兵宿衛，奏永寧宮。皇太后令敕臣如奏施行。臣輒敕主者及黃門令罷爽、羲、訓吏兵，以侯就第，不得逗留以稽車駕；敢有稽留，便以軍法從事。臣輒力疾，將兵屯洛水浮橋，伺察非常。」〔二〕

If there is a closing of the City Gates, who will again let you inside?” [Cáo] Shuǎng said: “Who would dare do so?” Because of this they no longer all together went. 〔一〕　世語曰：爽兄弟先是數俱出游，桓範謂曰：「總萬機，典禁兵，不宜並出，若有閉城門，誰復內入者？」爽曰：「誰敢爾邪！」由此不復並行。至是乃盡出也。

爽得宣王奏事，不通，迫窘不知所為。〔一〕大司農沛國桓範聞兵起，不應太后召，矯詔開平昌門，拔取劍戟，略將門候，南奔爽。宣王知，曰：「範畫策，爽必不能用範計。」範說爽使車駕幸許昌，招外兵。爽兄弟猶豫未決，範重謂羲曰：「當今日，卿門戶求貧賤復可得乎？且匹夫持質一人，尚欲望活，今卿與天子相隨，令於天下，誰敢不應者？」羲猶不能納。侍中許允、尚書陳泰說爽，使早自歸罪。爽於是遣允、泰詣宣王，歸罪請死，乃通宣王奏事。〔二〕遂免爽兄弟，以侯還第。〔三〕

〔一〕　干寶晉紀曰：爽留車駕宿伊水南，伐木為鹿角，發屯甲兵數千人以為衛。魏末傳曰：宣王語弟孚，陛下在外不可露宿，促送帳幔、太官食具詣行在所。













[33] Gān Bǎo’s Jìn shū states: Huán Fàn went out to go to [Cáo] Shuǎng, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng spoke to Jiǎng Jì stating: “The bag of wisdom has gone.” [Jiǎng] Jì said: “Fàn is indeed wise, but a worn out horse longs for stable beans, [Cáo] Shuǎng certainly is unable to employ him.”
Shìyǔ states: [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng sent Xǔ Yǔn and Chén Tài to explain to and speak with [Cáo] Shuǎng, Jiǎng Jì also sent a letter to explain [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s intentions, and also sent [Cáo] Shuǎng’s trusted Hall Central Colonel Yǐn Dàmù to speak with [Cáo] Shuǎng, that it would only remove his office and nothing more, with the Luò river as a pledge. [Cáo] Shuǎng trusted it and dismissed his troops.
Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: [Cáo] Shuǎng had dismissed his troops and said: “I will not lose out on being a wealthy old man.” [Huán] Fàn wept and said: “Cáo Zǐdān was a great man, but begat you brothers, mere sacrificial calves! How could one have imagined that today in connection to you all the clan would be exterminated!”



〔二〕　干寶晉書曰：桓範出赴爽，宣王謂蔣濟曰：「智囊往矣。」濟曰：「範則智矣，駑馬戀棧豆，爽必不能用也。」世語曰：宣王使許允、陳泰解語爽，蔣濟亦與書達宣王之旨，又使爽所信殿中校尉尹大目謂爽，唯免官而已，以洛水為誓。爽信之，罷兵。魏氏春秋曰：爽既罷兵，曰：「我不失作富家翁。」範哭曰：「曹子丹佳人，生汝兄弟，犢耳！何圖今日坐汝等族滅矣！」













[34] Wèi Mò zhuàn states: [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers returned home. Ordered Luòyáng county to mobilize civilians of eight hundred people, sending the Commandant division to surround [Cáo] Shuǎng’s mansion’s four corners, at each corner building a high tower, sending people to the top to watch the activities of [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers. [Cáo] Shuǎng’s plans were exhuated and he was in despair, holding a crossbow in arrived inside the Rear Garden, atop the towers people then chanted saying: “The former General-in-Chief goes southeast!” [Cáo] Shuǎng returned up to the office, with his brothers together discussed, not knowing how deep or shallow were [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s intentions, wrote a letter to [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng that said: “Despicable boy [Cáo] Shuǎng is in dread and terror, in insolence incurred disaster, rightfully should receive slaughter and extermination, formerly sent household servants to welcome provisions, to now they have not yet returned, for several days we have been lacking, and must bother you to seek rations, to go through dawn and dusk.” [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng obtained the letter and was greatly alarmed, at once sent answer letter that said: “Previously I was unaware that you lacked provisions, and extremely feel unsettled. Order to deliver rice of one hundred hú, together with dried meat, salted fermented beans, and soybeans.” It was quickly sent. [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers did not understand the changing situations, were immediately joyous, themselves saying they would not die.



〔三〕　魏末傳曰：爽兄弟歸家，敕洛陽縣發民八百人，使尉部圍爽第四角，角作高樓，令人在上望視爽兄弟舉動。爽計窮愁悶，持彈到後園中，樓上人便唱言「故大將軍東南行！」爽還廳事上，與兄弟共議，未知宣王意深淺，作書與宣王曰：「賤子爽哀惶恐怖，無狀招禍，分受屠滅，前遣家人迎糧，于今未反，數日乏匱，當煩見餉，以繼旦夕。」宣王得書大驚，即答書曰：「初不知乏糧，甚懷踧踖。令致米一百斛，并肉脯、鹽豉、大豆。」尋送。爽兄弟不達變數，即便喜歡，自謂不死。







Previously, Zhāng Dāng privately selected Talent Ladies Zhāng and Hé and others to send to [Cáo] Shuǎng. Suspecting illicit relations, arrested [Zhāng] Dāng to punish the crime. [Zhāng] Dāng testified [Cáo] Shuǎng with [Hé] Yàn and the rest had secretly plotted rebellion, and together in advance trained troops, to wait for during the Third Moon to mobilize. Thereupon arrested [Hé] Yàn and the rest and sent down to prison. Assembled the Excellencies and Ministers and Court Councilors at the Courtyard to discuss, they believed: “By the principles of the Chūnqiū, ‘The lord’s kin do not command, if they command then they must be executed.’ [Cáo] Shuǎng as a branch relation for generations was immerssed in exceptional favor, personally received the Former Emperor’s hand grasping Legacy Edict, entrusted with Heaven’s Under, but secretly harbored a disastrous heart, scorned and abandoned the legacy mandate, and so with [Hé] Yàn, [Dèng] Yáng, and [Zhāng] Dāng and the rest plotted for the Divine Vessels. [Huán] Fàn allied together with criminals. All are Great Rebellion Without Morality.” Thereupon arrested [Cáo] Shuǎng, [Cáo] Xī, [Cáo] Xùn, [Hé] Yàn, [Dèng] Yáng, [Dīng] Mì, [Bì] Guǐ, [Lǐ] Shèng, [Huán] Fàn, [Zāng] Dāng and others, all submitted to execution, exterminated Three Clans.98 [34] During Jiāpíng, to continue the lineages of meritorious ministers, enfeoffed [Cáo] Zhēn’s cousin’s grandson [Cáo] Xī as Marquess of Xīnchāng precinct, estate three hundred households, to serve as [Cáo] Zhēn’s posterity. [35]



初，張當私以所擇才人張、何等與爽。疑其有姦，收當治罪。當陳爽與晏等陰謀反逆，並先習兵，須三月中欲發，於是收晏等下獄。會公卿朝臣廷議，以為「春秋之義，『君親無將，將而必誅』。爽以支屬，世蒙殊寵，親受先帝握手遺詔，託以天下，而包藏禍心，蔑棄顧命，乃與晏、颺及當等謀圖神器，範黨同罪人，皆為大逆不道」。於是收爽、羲、訓、晏、颺、謐、軌、勝、範、當等，皆伏誅，夷三族。〔一〕嘉平中，紹功臣世，封真族孫熙為新昌亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉真後。〔二〕










[34] Wèi lüè states:
Dèng Yáng appellation Xuánmào was Dèng Yǔ’s posterity. As a youth he obtained a serviceman’s reputation in the capital region. In Emperor Míng’s time he became a Secretariat Writers Cadet, appointed Luòyáng Magistrate, in connection to a matter was dismissed, appointed Central Cadet, also entered as a concurrent Central Writers Cadet. Previously, [Dèng] Yáng with Lǐ Shèng and others were superficial and pretentious friends, reaching to when he was in the Central Writers, the superficial and pretentious matters were discovered, he was expelled out, and therefore no longer employed. At Zhèngshǐ’s beginning, then he was sent out as Yǐngchuān Administrator, transferred to General-in-Chief’s Chief Clerk, promoted to Attendant Central Secretariat Writer. [Dèng] Yáng as a man enjoyed money, formerly when in an inner office, he promised Zāng Ài a conferment with a prominent office, [Zāng] Ài had his father’s concubine given to [Dèng] Yáng, therefore the capital region made it into a saying that stated: “For an office exchange a woman to Dèng Xuánmào.” Of all those that he recommended and promoted, many were comparable to this. Therefore Hé Yàn in selections and recommendations not finding appropriate people tended to be due to [Dèng] Yáng’s lack of fairnes and loyalty, thus they shared in the same crimes, overall because of associating with friends of improper talents.
Dīng Mì appellation Yànjìng. His father [Dīng] Fěi appellation Wénhóu. Previously, [Dīng] Fěi accompanied Tàizǔ, Tàizǔ because [Dīng] Fěi was of the same hometown specially tolerated and favored him. [Dīng] Fěi by nature enjoyed money, repeatedly made requests and violated laws, at once obtained pardon and forgiveness. Became Organizing Army Colonel, presiding over interior and exterior, of all that he explained and advised, many were followed. At Jiàn’ān’s end, he followed Tàizǔ on campaign against Wú. [Dīng] Fěi while accompanying himself believed his family ox was lean and exhausted, and so privately exchanged it for a government ox, was reported by someone, and was arrested and sent to prison, taking away his office. Afterward Tàizǔ asked [Dīng] Fěi stating: “Wénhóu, where are your seal and ribbon?” [Dīng] Fěi also knew he was being teased, and replied stating: “I merely exchanged it for pastry.” Tàizǔ laughed, looked back to speak with his Left and Right stating: ” East Department Assistant Máo repeatedly reported this family, wishing to have me heavily punish. It is not that I do not know this man is not pure, it is there is a good reason to keep him. My keeping of [Dīng] Fěi is like a family having a thieving dog that yet excels at catching rats. Though the thefts are a small loss, yet it preserves my purse stores.” Therefore restored [Dīng] Fěi’s office, listening to and employing him as before. After several years he died of illness. [Dīng] Mì as a youth would not agree to socialize, only widely reading books and commentaries. As a many he was deep and resolute, and considerably had talent and strategy. During Tàihé, he once stayed at Yè, borrowed someone’s empty room, resided inside it, but some kings also wished to borrow it, did not know [Dīng] Mì had already obtained it, and directly opened the gate to enter. [Dīng] Mì looked and saw the kings, laid down with crossed legs and did not rise, and called his slaves and retainers stating: “Who are these people? Quickly scold them to have them leave.” the kings were angry at his lack of respect, returned and sent up report of his words. Emperor Míng arrested [Dīng] Mì, bound in Yè prison, but as he was an accomplished minister’s son, pardoned and released him. Later the Emperor heard he had resemblance to his father, summoned and appointed him Limiting Expenses Cadet Central. Cáo Shuǎng had long been close with him, at the time when [Cáo] Shuǎng was Martial Guard General, he repeatedly praised him to the Emperor as capable of great use. It happened that the Emperor passed away, [Cáo] Shuǎng assisted in government, thust selected out [Dīng] Mì as Cavalier Regular Attendant, then transferred to Secretariat Writer. [Dīng] Mì as a man outside appeared careless and negligent but inside was often suspicious and calculating. When at the Terrace Pavillions, he repeatedly made impeachments and denunciations, those in the Terrace suffered from it, matters could not be enacted. Also he thought little of nobility, many were neglected by him, although he with Hé Yàn and Dèng Yáng and the rest were of the same rank, yet he thought little of them all, only due to power deferred to [Cáo] Shuǎng. [Cáo] Shuǎng also respected him, of his advice none was not followed. Therefore at the time there was a slanderous letter saying: “Inside the Terrace there are three dogs, two dogs snarling99 and cannot be matched, one dog relying on silence (Mò) to become an ulcer sack.” Three dogs was speaking of Hé [Yàn], Dèng [Yáng], Dīng [Mì]. Mò (silence) was [Cáo] Shuǎng’s childhood appellation. Its meaning was to say that the three dogs all wished to bite people, but [Dīng] Mì was the most extreme. Memorializing to send Dowager Empress Guō out to reside in a separate Palace, and sending the King of Lè’ān to go north to visit Yè, and also sending Wén Qīn to return to Huáinán, all were [Dīng] Mì’s plans. Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng because of this especially deeply hated him.
Bì Guǐ appellation Zhāoxiān. His father appellation Zǐlǐ, during Jiàn’ān became a Managing Agriculture Colonel. [Bì] Guǐ for talent and ability from youth had fame. At the time when Emperor Míng was at the East Palace, [Bì] Guǐ was among his Literary Scholars. At Huángchū’s end, he was sent out as a Chief Scribe. When Emperor Míng succeeded the throne, entered as a Yellow Gate Cadet, his son bestowed a princess, lived in prosperity and wealth. Promoted to Bìng Province Inspector. At Bìng Province he had a reputation for arrogance and indulgence. At the time miscellaneous caitiffs repeatedly made violence, harming clerks and civilians, [Bì] Guǐ at once sent out the army to strike Xiānbēi Kē Bǐnéng, was unsuccessful. Central Protector of the Army Jiǎng Jì memorialized stating: “Bì Guǐ’s former failures are already past and need not be blamed, one only fears from this afterwards it is difficult to allow a repeat. Overall human talents have their strengths and shortcomings, and cannot be forced into success. [Bì] Guǐ’s literary refinement and willful intention assuredly make him a fine vessel. Now in losing Bìng Province, he should be switched to be installed to another province, or enter to occupy a prominent position, to not defame his virtue, for state affairs it truly would be good. This is vital to security or danger, may Your Sagely Grace investigate it.” Reaching to during Zhèngshǐ, he entered as Central Protector of the Army, transferred to Attendant Central Secretariat Writer, promoted to Director of Retainers Colonel. Formerly he was friendly with Cáo Shuǎng, every time in advising [Cáo] Shuǎng, many times it was followed.
Lǐ Shèng appellation Gōngzhāo. His father [Lǐ] Xiū appellation Zǐlǎng had wisdom and strategy. Zhāng Lǔ formerly was Defending North General, [Lǐ] Xiū was his Major, family at Nánzhèng. At the time Hànzhōng had sweet dew fall, Zǐlǎng saw Zhāng Lǔ had elite troops of several tens of thousands of men, had the firmness of a four-sided stronghold, and therefore established advice that the Red Aura had long declined, the Yellow House would rise, wishing for [Zhāng] Lǔ to claim title, [Zhāng] Lǔ did not listen. It happened that [Zhāng] Lǔ was defeated, Tàizǔ because he had urged [Zhāng] Lǔ to inwardly attach, bestowed noble title as Marquess Within the Passes, installed Irregular Office Cavalry Follower, to visit Yè. Reaching to during Huángchū, he served successively as Administrator of Shàngdǎng and Jùlù two prefectures, later due to old age returned, appointed Consultant Cadet. [Lǐ] Shèng in youth roamed the capital region, elegant and having talent and wisdom, friendly with Cáo Shuǎng. Emperor Míng banned the superficial and pretentious, and someone reported that [Lǐ] Shèng’s halls had the Four Windows and Eight Convances, each having a designated name. Using this he was arrested, those that were connected and cited were many, therefore he obtained pardon, banned from office for several years. The Emperor passed away, Cáo Shuǎng assisted in government, [Lǐ] Shèng became Luòyáng Magistrate. When Xiàhóu Xuán became Campaigning West General, appointed [Lǐ] Shèng as his Chief Scribe. [Xiàhóu] Xuán also had long had a strong relationship with [Lǐ] Shèng. In the Luò valley campaign, many of the followed suggestions were produced by [Lǐ] Shèng, because of this Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng was displeased with [Lǐ] Shèng. Gradually promoted to Xíngyáng Administrator, Hénán Intendant. [Lǐ] Shèng beginning to end in his government administrations never once was not praised in office. He was Intendant for over a year, in front of the office the túsū was broken,100 ordered people to again repair it, small timber of one piece suddenly fell, directly striking a receiving tally clerk Shí Hǔ’s head, breaking it. Later in ten days he was promoted to Jīng Province Inspector, had not yet reached the office and was destroyed.
Huán Fàn appellation Yuánzé for generations was of dominant clan. At Jiàn’ān’s end, he entered the Assistant Chancellor’s Office. During Yánkāng, he became Feather Forest Left Overseer. As he had literary talent, with Wáng Xiàng and others he managed the compilation of the Huánglǎn. In Emperor Míng’s time he became Central Manager of the Army and Secretariat Writer, promoted to Campaigning against Caitiffs General, East Central Cadet General, Envoy Holding Stave as Overall Supervisor of Qīng and Xú various military affairs, headquarters at Xiàpī. With Xú Province Inspector Zhèng Qí he fought over housing, drew his Stave wishing to behead [Zhèng] Qí, was memorialized against by [Zhèng] Qí as unjust, in connection was dismissed and returned. Reappointed as Yǎn Province Inspector, he was discontented and unable to obtain his wishes. Also he heard he was to be transferred to Jì Province Governor. At the time Jì Province was subordinate to the Defending North, and Defending North General Lǚ Zhāo in true talent and service advancement had originally been behind [Huán] Fàn. [Huán] Fàn spoke to his wife Zhòngcháng101 stating: “I would rather be in the Ministers, only kneeling toward the Three Excellencies. I cannot bend to Lǚ Zǐzhǎn.” His wife said: “You formerly were in the east, in connection to wishing to usurp authority to execute the Xú Province Inspector, everyone said you were difficult to serve as a subordinate. Now you are again ashamed to bend to Lǚ, it is to also be difficult to be your superior.” [Huán] Fàn was arranged her words touched on the truth, and so with a saber pommel struck her abdomen. The wife at the time was pregnant, and therefore miscarried and died. [Huán] Fàn also indeed claimed illness, not going to Jì Province. During Zhèngshǐ he was appointed Minister of Agriculture. [Huán] Fàn formerly was at the Terrace Pavillions, acclaimed for understanding affairs, reaching to becoming Minister of Agriculture, he also for purity and frugality was praised. [Huán] Fàn once selected and compiled various miscellaneous events in the Hàn shū, by his own opinions edited it, titled as Shìyāo lùn (“Discourse on Essentials of the Age”). Jiǎng Jì was Grand Commandant, once with [Huán] Fàn gathered below the altars, the various ministers lined in seats were several people, [Huán] Fàn had his compilation in his bosom, wished to show it to [Jiăng] Jì, saying [Jiǎng] Jì would be open-minded and read it. [Huán] Fàn produced his book to show the Left and Right, the Left and Right passed it to show to [Jiǎng] Jì, [Jiǎng] Jì would not agree to look at it, [Huán] Fàn in his heart resented this. Taking advantage of a discussion of another matter, then he angrily spoke to [Jiǎng] Jì stating: “My ancestors were meager in virtue, but how can Your Excellency’s generation compare?” Although [Jiǎng] Jì by nature was strong and resolute, he also knew [Huán] Fàn was stubborn and resolute, looked aside and did not answer, and each departed. When [Huán] Fàn was in Pèi prefecture his service sequence was after Cáo Zhēn. At the time Cáo Shuǎng assisted in government, as [Huán] Fàn was an elder of his hometown, among the Nine Ministers he was especially respectful to him, however they were not very close. Reaching to when [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng raised troops, closing the city gates, as [Huán] Fàn had understanding in affairs, thus directed to summon him, wishing to send him as designate Central Manager of the Army.102 [Huán] Fàn wished to answer the summons, but his son remonstrated him, believing as the Chariot Carriage was outside, it was not as good as going out south. [Huán] Fàn hesitated for a moment, and his son again hurried him. [Huán] Fàn wished to leave but the Minister of Agriculture’s deputies and clerks all stopped [Huán] Fàn. [Huán] Fàn did not listen, and so rushed out to reach Píngchāng City Gate. The City Gate was already closed. Gate Guard Sī Fán was a former clerk recommended by [Huán] Fàn. [Huán] Fàn callled to him, raising a register in his hand to show him, falsely stating: “There is Edict summoning me, you quickly open the gates!” [Sī] Fán wished to request to see the Edict letter, [Huán] Fàn scolded him, saying: “Are you not my former clerk? How dare you act like this?” Thus opened it. [Huán] Fàn exited the city, turned back and spoke to [Sī] Fán stating: “The Grand Tutor plots rebellion, you follow us and go!” [Sī] Fán on foot travelled and could not catch up, and therefore stepped aside. [Huán] Fàn went south and met [Cáo] Shuǎng, urged [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers to have Heaven’s Son visit Xǔchāng, and summon the Four Quarters to support themselves. [Cáo] Shuǎng was doubtful, [Cáo] Xī also did not speak. [Huán] Fàn himself spoke to [Cáo] Xī stating: “The situation is clear, what use was your reading of books for? Today your household has fallen!” Both did not speak. [Huán] Fàn again spoke to [Cáo] Xī stating: “Your separate camp is nearby to the south of the watchtowers, Luòyáng’s Manager of Agriculture headquarters is outside the city walls, your calls and summons will be as you wish. Now to visit Xǔchāng is to not take more than a night, Xǔchāng’s separate storehouses are sufficient for temporary supply. The only concern is in grain and provisions, but the seal and insignia of the Minister of Agriculture is on my person.” [Cáo] Xī and his brothers were silent and did not follow this. In the middle of the night reaching the fifth watch,103 [Cáo] Shuǎng then threw his saber to the ground, speaking to the various ministers following the Carriage stating: “I judge the Grand Tutor’s intention is also no more than to wish to have me and my brothers submit to him. I alone have merely not accorded to the far and near.” Therefore he advanced to speak to the Emperor stating: “Your Majesty should make an Edict to dismiss Your Servant from office, and reply to the Imperial Dowager Empress’s Order.” [Huán] Fàn knew if [Cáo] Shuǎng was first to request dismissal then he himself would certainly be connected to inciting an uprising. [Huán] Fàn thus said: “Old man that I am, now in connection to you brothers my clan is exterminated!” [Cáo] Shuǎng and the rest had been dismissed, the Emperor returned to the Palace, therefore ordered [Huán] Fàn to accompany. Arriving at the Luò river pontonn bridge’s north, he looked out and saw [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng, dismounted charriage and knocked head and was without speech. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng called [Huán] Fàn by his surname stating: “Grandee Huán why be like this?” The Chariot Carriage entered the Palace, there was Edict for [Huán] Fàn to return and be restored to his position. [Huán] Fàn visited the watchtowers to bow and submit Reply of thanks, and waited for reply. It happened that Sī Fán had visited the Minister Herald to surrender himself, and entirely said what [Huán] Fàn had explained before setting out. [Sīmǎ Yì] Then was furious and said: “Falsely accusing someone of rebellion, by the law what is the answer?” The manager said: “By the law, they instead receive the punishment.” Thus arrested [Huán] Fàn below the watchtowers. At the time the people grabbing [Huán] Fàn were extremely hurried, [Huán] Fàn spoke to the division officials stating: “Slow down, I also am merely a righteous serviceman.” Therefore sent to the Minster of Justice.
Shìyǔ states: Previously, [Cáo] Shuǎng dreamed of two tigers holding the God of Thunder in their mouths, the God of Thunder resembling a two shēng bowl, released and placed in a courtyard. [Cáo] Shuǎng hated this, and asked a diviner about it. Língtái104 Deputy Mǎ Xùn said: “Worry of troops.” [Mǎ] Xùn withdrew, and reported to his wife stating: “[Cáo] Shuǎng will by troops perish, in no more than ten days.”
Hàn Jìn Chūnqiū states: Āndìng’s Huángfǔ Mì in the Ninth Year winter dreamed of reaching Luòyáng, from a temple exiting, saw the chariots and riders were extremely many, with an object presented to the temple saying: “Executed General-in-Chief Cáo Shuǎng.” He awoke and told this his villagers. The villagers said: “You wish to be the dreamer of the Cáo men? But what if the Court is without a Gōngsūn Qiáng?105 Moreover [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers manage heavy troops, and also control Secretariat Writers affairs, who dares plan against them?” [Huángfǔ] Mì said: “[Cáo] Shuǎng is without Shūzhènduó’s pleading,106 if he loses Heaven’s mechanisms then he is isolated, how can he rely on strength? In the past Hàn’s Yán Xiǎn relied on the honor of the Mother Dowager, wielded power over the state’s authority and mandates, what can be called the utmost heaviest, but castrates of nineteen people in one morning made him a corpse,107 all the more for [Cáo] Shuǎng and his brothers.”
Shìyǔ states: Previously, [Cáo] Shuǎng went out, his Major Lǔ Zhī remained at the office, heard there was a situation, commanded camp cavalry to chop through Jīn Gate to go out to go to [Cáo] Shuǎng. When [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed, he was selected out to be Censorate Central Deputy. When [Cáo] Shuǎng untied his seal and ribbon, about to go out, his Registrar Yáng Zōng stopped him stating: “Your Excellency holds the Ruler and grasps the reins,108, are you abandoning this to go to the East Market?”109 [Cáo] Shuǎng did not follow this. Relevant managers memorialized that [Yáng] Zōng had directed [Cáo] Shuǎng to rebel, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng said: “Each has their master.” Pardoned him, appointed Secretariat Writers Cadet. [Lǔ] Zhī appellation Shìyīng was a Fúfēng man. For later service he advanced to reach Specially Advanced Radiant Grandee. [Yáng] Zōng appellation Chūbó, later became Securing East General Sīmǎ [Zhāo] Wén-wáng’s Chief Scribe.
Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: Xiàhóu Zhàn’s engraving for [Lǔ] Zhī and Gān Bǎo’s Jìn jì both say that when [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng then selected out [Lǔ] Zhī to be Bìng Province Inspector, and [Yáng] Zōng became Securing East Advisor to the Army. It is not in agreement with Shìyǔ.



〔一〕　魏略曰：鄧颺字玄茂，鄧禹後也。少得士名於京師。明帝時為尚書郎，除洛陽令，坐事免，拜中郎，又入兼中書郎。初，颺與李勝等為浮華友，及在中書，浮華事發，被斥出，遂不復用。正始初，乃出為潁川太守，轉大將軍長史，遷侍中尚書。颺為人好貨，前在內職，許臧艾授以顯官，艾以父妾與颺，故京師為之語曰：「以官易婦鄧玄茂。」每所薦達，多如此比。故何晏選舉不得人，頗由颺之不公忠，遂同其罪，蓋由交友非其才。丁謐，字彥靖。父斐，字文侯。初，斐隨太祖，太祖以斐鄉里，特饒愛之。斐性好貨，數請求犯法，輒得原宥。為典軍校尉，總攝內外，每所陳說，多見從之。建安末，從太祖征吳。斐隨行，自以家牛羸困，乃私易官牛，為人所白，被收送獄，奪官。其後太祖問斐曰：「文侯，印綬所在？」斐亦知見戲，對曰：「以易餅耳。」太祖笑，顧謂左右曰：「東曹毛掾數白此家，欲令我重治，我非不知此人不清，良有以也。我之有斐，譬如人家有盜狗而善捕鼠，盜雖有小損，而完我囊貯。」遂復斐官，聽用如初。後數歲，病亡。謐少不肯交游，但博觀書傳。為人沈毅，頗有才略。太和中，常住鄴，借人空屋，居其中。而諸王亦欲借之，不知謐已得，直開門入。謐望見王，交腳臥而不起，而呼其奴客曰：「此何等人？促呵使去。」王怒其無禮，還具上言。明帝收謐，繫鄴獄，以其功臣子，原出。後帝聞其有父風，召拜度支郎中。曹爽宿與相親，時爽為武衛將軍，數為帝稱其可大用。會帝崩，爽輔政，乃拔謐為散騎常侍，遂轉尚書。謐為人外似疏略，而內多忌。其在臺閣，數有所彈駮，臺中患之，事不得行。又其意輕貴，多所忽略，雖與何晏、鄧颺等同位，而皆少之，唯以勢屈於爽。爽亦敬之，言無不從。故于時謗書，謂「臺中有三狗，二狗崖柴不可當，一狗憑默作疽囊。」三狗，謂何、鄧、丁也。默者，爽小字也。其意言三狗皆欲嚙人，而謐尤甚也。奏使郭太后出居別宮，及遣樂安王使北詣鄴，又遣文欽令還淮南，皆謐之計。司馬宣王由是特深恨之。畢軌，字昭先。父字子禮，建安中為典農校尉。軌以才能，少有名聲。明帝在東宮時，軌在文學中。黃初末，出為長史。明帝即位，入為黃門郎，子尚公主，居處殷富。遷并州刺史。其在并州，名為驕豪。時雜虜數為暴，害吏民，軌輒出軍擊鮮卑軻比能，失利。中護軍蔣濟表曰：「畢軌前失，既往不咎，但恐是後難可以再。凡人材有長短，不可彊成。軌文雅志意，自為美器。今失并州，換置他州，若入居顯職，不毀其德，於國事實善。此安危之要，唯聖恩察之。」至正始中，入為中護軍，轉侍中尚書，遷司隸校尉。素與曹爽善，每言於爽，多見從之。李勝字公昭。父休字子朗，有智略。張魯前為鎮北將軍，休為司馬，家南鄭。時漢中有甘露降，子朗見張魯精兵數萬人，有四塞之固，遂建言赤氣久衰，黃家當興，欲魯舉號，魯不聽。會魯破，太祖以其勸魯內附，賜爵關內侯，署散官騎從，詣鄴。至黃初中，仕歷上黨、鉅鹿二郡太守，後以年老還，拜議郎。勝少游京師，雅有才智，與曹爽善。明帝禁浮華，而人白勝堂有四窗八達，各有主名。用是被收，以其所連引者多，故得原，禁錮數歲。帝崩，曹爽輔政，勝為洛陽令。夏侯玄為征西將軍，以勝為長史。玄亦宿與勝厚。駱谷之役，議從勝出，由是司馬宣王不悅於勝。累遷滎陽太守、河南尹。勝前後所宰守，未嘗不稱職，為尹歲餘，廳事前屠蘇壞，令人更治之，小材一枚激墮，正撾受符吏石虎頭，斷之。後旬日，遷為荊州刺史，未及之官而敗也。桓範字元則，世為冠族。建安末，入丞相府。延康中，為羽林左監。以有文學，與王象等典集皇覽。明帝時為中領軍尚書，遷征虜將軍、東中郎將，使持節都督青、徐諸軍事，治下邳。與徐州刺史鄭岐爭屋，引節欲斬岐，為岐所奏，不直，坐免還。復為兗州刺吏，怏怏不得意。又聞當轉為冀州牧。是時冀州統屬鎮北，而鎮北將軍呂昭才實仕進，本在範後。範謂其妻仲長曰：「我寧作諸卿，向三公長跪耳，不能為呂子展屈也。」其妻曰：「君前在東，坐欲擅斬徐州刺史，眾人謂君難為作下，今復羞為呂屈，是復難為作上也。」範忿其言觸實，乃以刀環撞其腹。妻時懷孕，遂墮胎死。範亦竟稱疾，不赴冀州。正始中拜大司農。範前在臺閣，號為曉事，及為司農，又以清省稱。範嘗抄撮漢書中諸雜事，自以意斟酌之，名曰世要論。蔣濟為太尉，嘗與範會社下，群卿列坐有數人，範懷其所撰，欲以示濟，謂濟當虛心觀之。範出其書以示左右，左右傳之示濟，濟不肯視，範心恨之。因論他事，乃發怒謂濟曰：「我祖薄德，公輩何似邪？」濟性雖彊毅，亦知範剛毅，睨而不應，各罷。範於沛郡，仕次在曹真後。于時曹爽輔政，以範鄉里老宿，於九卿中特敬之，然不甚親也。及宣王起兵，閉城門，以範為曉事，乃指召之，欲使領中領軍。範欲應召，而其子諫之，以車駕在外，不如南出。範疑有頃，兒又促之。範欲去而司農丞吏皆止範。範不從，乃突出至平昌城門，城門已閉。門候司蕃，故範舉吏也，範呼之，舉手中版以示之，矯曰：「有詔召我，卿促開門！」蕃欲求見詔書，範呵之，言「卿非我故吏邪，何以敢爾？」乃開之。範出城，顧謂蕃曰：「太傅圖逆，卿從我去！」蕃徒行不能及，遂避側。範南見爽，勸爽兄弟以天子詣許昌，徵四方以自輔。爽疑，羲又無言。範自謂羲曰：「事昭然，卿用讀書何為邪！於今日卿等門戶倒矣！」俱不言。範又謂羲曰：「卿別營近在闕南，洛陽典農治在城外，呼召如意。今詣許昌，不過中宿，許昌別庫，足相被假；所憂當在穀食，而大司農印章在我身。」羲兄弟默然不從，中夜至五鼓，爽乃投刀于地，謂諸從駕群臣曰：「我度太傅意，亦不過欲令我兄弟向己也。我獨有以不合于遠近耳！」遂進謂帝曰：「陛下作詔免臣官，報皇太后令。」範知爽首免而己必坐唱義也。範乃曰：「老子今茲坐卿兄弟族矣！」爽等既免，帝還宮，遂令範隨從。到洛水浮橋北，望見宣王，下車叩頭而無言。宣王呼範姓曰：「桓大夫何為爾邪！」車駕入宮，有詔範還復位。範詣闕拜章謝，待報。會司蕃詣鴻臚自首，具說範前臨出所道。宣王乃忿然曰：「誣人以反，於法何應？」主者曰：「科律，反受其罪。」乃收範於闕下。時人持範甚急，範謂部官曰：「徐之，我亦義士耳。」遂送廷尉。世語曰：初，爽夢二虎銜雷公，雷公若二升碗，放著庭中。爽惡之，以問占者，靈臺丞馬訓曰：「憂兵。」訓退，告其妻曰：「爽將以兵亡，不出旬日。」漢晉春秋曰：安定皇甫謐以九年冬夢至洛陽，自廟出，見車騎甚眾，以物呈廟云：「誅大將軍曹爽。」寤而以告其邑人，邑人曰：「君欲作曹人之夢乎！朝無公孫彊如何？且爽兄弟典重兵，又權尚書事，誰敢謀之？」謐曰：「爽無叔振鐸之請，苟失天機則離矣，何恃于彊？昔漢之閻顯，倚母后之尊，權國威命，可謂至重矣，閹人十九人一旦尸之，況爽兄弟乎？」世語曰：初，爽出，司馬魯芝留在府，聞有事，將營騎斫津門出赴爽。爽誅，擢為御史中丞。及爽解印綬，將出，主簿楊綜止之曰：「公挾主握灌，捨此以至東巿乎？」爽不從。有司奏綜導爽反，宣王曰：「各為其主也。」宥之，以為尚書郎。芝字世英，扶風人也。以後仕進至特進光祿大夫。綜字初伯，後為安東將軍司馬文王長史。臣松之案：夏侯湛為芝銘及干寶晉紀並云爽既誅，宣王即擢芝為并州刺史，以綜為安東參軍。與世語不同。

〔二〕　干寶晉紀曰：蔣濟以曹真之勳力，不宜絕祀，故以熙為後。濟又病其言之失信于爽，發病卒。






Hé Yàn


[Hé] Yàn was Hé Jìn’s grandson. His mother Yǐn-shì became Tàizǔ’s consort. [Hé] Yàn grew up in the Palace offices, also was bestowed a princess, from youth for his abundant talent was famed, enjoyed Lǎo-Zhuāng philosophy,110 wrote the Dào Dé lùn111 and various essays, rhapsodies, and writings altogether several tens of fascicle. [36]



晏，何進孫也。母尹氏，為太祖夫人。晏長于宮省，又尚公主，少以才秀知名，好老莊言，作道德論及諸文賦著述凡數十篇。〔一〕










[36] [Hé] Yàn appellation Píngshū.
Wèilüè states: At the time when Tàizǔ was Excellency of Works, he accepted (as concubine) [Hé] Yàn’s mother and also adopted [Hé] Yàn, at the time Qín Yílù’s son Ā’sū also accompanied his mother and was in the Excellency’s house, both met with favor like the Excellency’s sons. Sū was [Qín] Lǎng. [Qín] Sū by nature was cautious, but [Hé] Yàn was without any consideration or fears, his clothes and adornments imitated the Heir-Apparent, therefore Emperor Wén specially detested him, never calling him by family name or appellation, always calling him as “the adopted son.” [Hé] Yàn was bestowed a princess, also enjoyed lechery, therefore in the time of Huángchū he was without duties or appointments. Reaching to Emperor Míng’s establishment, he tended to be in the Redundant Officials.112 Reaching the beginning of Zhèngshǐ, he accomodated to Cáo Shuǎng, and also had talent and capability, therefore [Cáo] Shuǎng employed him as Cavalier Regular Attendant, promoted to Attendant Central Secretariat Writer. [Hé] Yàn formerly due to being bestowed a princess was able to be bestowed noble title as a Ranked Marquess, also his mother was inside (the Palace), [Hé] Yàn by nature was self-satisfied, whether moving or at rest white (makeup) powder did not leave his hand, while walking he looked back at his own shadow. [Hé] Yàn became a Secretariat Writer, managed selections and recommendations, of those that had former old relationships with him, many were selected out for promotion.
Wèi Mò zhuàn states: [Hé] Yàn’s wife was the Princess of Jīnxiāng, [Hé] Yàn’s younger (half) sister of the same mother.113 The princess was worthy, and spoke to her mother the King of Pèi’s Dowager stating: “[Hé] Yàn evildoing daily grows more extreme, how will he protect himself?” Her mother laughed and said: “Are you perhaps jealous of [Hé] Yàn?” Shortly afterwards [Hé] Yàn died. He had one son, aged five to six years, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng sent someone to arrest him. [Hé] Yàn’s mother took and hid the child inside the King’s Palace, faced the envoy and beat her own cheeks, begging to spare him. The envoy reported the situation to [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng also had heard that [Hé] Yàn’s wife had spoken with foresight, his heart always commended this, and moreover due to the King of Pèi, specially pardoned and did not kill.114
Wèi shì Chūnqiū states: Previously, Xiàhóu Xuán, Hé Yàn and others had fame flourishing at the time, Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng also participated with them. [Hé] Yàn once said: “‘Only by depth is one therefore capable of understanding the will of Heaven’s Under,’ Xiàhóu Tàichū is this. ‘Only by subtlety is one therefore capable of completing the tasks of Heaven’s Under,’ Sīmǎ Zǐyuán is this. ‘Only by divinity, is to not hurry and yet be fast, to not walk and yet arrive,’ I have heard of this saying, but not yet seen the person.”115 Probably he wished to use divinity to refer to himself. Previously, [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng had [Hé] Yàn participate in the investigation of the prison cases of [Cáo] Shuǎng and the rest. [Hé] Yàn exhaustively investigated the faction participants, hoping to by this obtain pardon. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng said: “Altogether there are eight clans.” [Hé] Yàn listed Dīng and Dèng and the rest of seven surnames. [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng said: “Not yet.” [Hé] Yàn was thoroughly anxious and so said: “Are you speaking of [me, Hé] Yàn?” [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng said: “Yes.” Thus arrested [Hé] Yàn.
Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: Wèi Mò zhuàn says that [Hé] Yàn took his younger sister of the same mother as wife. This is something the gentry116 would not bear to speak of, even the King of Chǔ taking as wife his brother’s widow is not this extreme. Even if this report had been produced from an old history, yet still one would not believe it, all the more for a base and inferior book. According to the biographies of the various Kings and Dukes, the King of Pèi was begat by the Lady Dù. [Hé] Yàn’s surname was Yǐn, if the princess with the King of Pèi were of the same mother, how could it be said she and [Hé] Yàn had the same mother?117
Huángfǔ Mì’s Liè Nǚ zhuàn states: [Cáo] Shuăng’s younger cousin Wénshū’s wife was Qiáo prefecture’s Xiàhóu Wénníng’s daughter, named Língnǚ. Wénshū early died, the mourning completed, she herself believed her years were few and she was without children, feared her family would certainly remarry her, and so cut her hair as a pledge. Afterwards her family indeed wished to marry her off, Língnǚ heard, and immediately again used a knife to cut her two ears, her residence always depended on [Cáo] Shuǎng. Reaching to when [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed, the Cáo clan was completely dead. Língnǚ’s father’s younger brother sent up letter to sever marriage ties with the Cáo clan, and forcefully welcomed Língnǚ to return home. At the time Wénníng was Liáng Chancellor, pitied her youth and maintaining of righteousness, and also the Cáo clan had no remaining survivors, hoped her intentions would end, and so secretly someone to hint to her. Língnǚ sighed and sobbed stating: “I also consider this, agreeing to it is correct.” The family believed it true, and their guarding became slightly lax. Língnǚ thereupon secretly entered the bedroom, with a knife cut off her nose, covered with a quilt and lay down. Her mother called her to speak, she did not answer, lifting the quilt and seeing her, the blood flow filled the bed and mat. The entire family was alarmed and rushed to go see her, none were not aching in nose. Someone spoke to her stating: “A person’s life in this world is like mere light dust perched on weak grass, why utmostly suffer like this? Moreover your husband’s family is already exterminated completely, maintaining this desire is for whom?” Língnǚ said: “I have heard benevolence is to not by flourishing or decline change integrity, righteousness is not to by survival or destruction change heart. At the time when the Cáo clan was formerly flourishing, still I wished to maintain to the end, all the more now when declined and destroyed, how can I bear to abandon it? The conduct of birds and beasts, how can I do it?” Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng heard and commended this, listened to and permitted her request for a child to adopt to be the Cáo clan’s posterity, her name famed in the world.



〔一〕　晏字平叔。魏略曰：「太祖為司空時，納晏母并收養晏，其時秦宜祿兒阿蘇亦隨母在公家，並見寵如公子。蘇即朗也。蘇性謹慎，而晏無所顧憚，服飾擬於太子，故文帝特憎之，每不呼其姓字，嘗謂之為「假子」。晏尚主，又好色，故黃初時無所事任。及明帝立，頗為冗官。至正始初，曲合于曹爽，亦以才能，故爽用為散騎侍郎，遷侍中尚書。晏前以尚主，得賜爵為列侯，又其母在內，晏性自喜，動靜粉白不去手，行步顧影。晏為尚書，主選舉，其宿與之有舊者，多被拔擢。魏末傳曰：晏婦金鄉公主，即晏同母妹。公主賢，謂其母沛王太妃曰：「晏為惡日甚，將何保身？」母笑曰：「汝得無妒晏邪！」俄而晏死。有一男，年五六歲，宣王遣人錄之。晏母歸藏其子王宮中，向使者搏頰，乞白活之，使者具以白宣王。宣王亦聞晏婦有先見之言，心常嘉之；且為沛王故，特原不殺。魏氏春秋曰：初，夏侯玄、何晏等名盛於時，司馬景王亦預焉。晏嘗曰：「唯深也，故能通天下之志，夏侯泰初是也；唯幾也，故能成天下之務，司馬子元是也；惟神也，不疾而速，不行而至，吾聞其語，未見其人。」蓋欲以神況諸己也。初，宣王使晏與治爽等獄。晏窮治黨與，冀以獲宥。宣王曰：「凡有八族。」晏疏丁、鄧等七姓。宣王曰：「未也。」晏窮急，乃曰：「豈謂晏乎！」宣王曰：「是也。」乃收晏。臣松之案：魏末傳云晏取其同母妹為妻，此搢紳所不忍言，雖楚王之妻（嫂）〔媦〕，不是甚也已。設令此言出于舊史，猶將莫之或信，況底下之書乎！案諸王公傳，沛王出自杜夫人所生。晏母姓尹，公主若與沛王同生，焉得言與晏同母？皇甫謐列女傳曰：爽從弟文叔，妻譙郡夏侯文寧之女，名令女。文叔早死，服闋，自以年少無子，恐家必嫁己，乃斷髮以為信。其後，家果欲嫁之，令女聞，即復以刀截兩耳，居止常依爽。及爽被誅，曹氏盡死。令女叔父上書與曹氏絕婚，彊迎令女歸。時文寧為梁相，憐其少，執義，又曹氏無遺類，冀其意沮，迺微使人諷之。令女歎且泣曰：「吾亦惟之，許之是也。」家以為信，防之少懈。令女於是竊入寢室，以刀斷鼻，蒙被而臥。其母呼與語，不應，發被視之，血流滿床席。舉家驚惶，奔往視之，莫不酸鼻。或謂之曰：「人生世間，如輕塵棲弱草耳，何至辛苦迺爾！且夫家夷滅已盡，守此欲誰為哉？」令女曰：「聞仁者不以盛衰改節，義者不以存亡易心，曹氏前盛之時，尚欲保終，況今衰亡，何忍棄之！禽獸之行，吾豈為乎？」司馬宣王聞而嘉之，聽使乞子字養，為曹氏後，名顯于世。
crumbs: 9  Biographies of the various Xiàhóu and Cáo

title: 9  Biographies of the various Xiàhóu and Cáo
text:
Xiàhóu Shàng


Xiàhóu Shàng appellation Bórén was [Xiàhóu] Yuān’s cousin’s son. Emperor Wén was close friends with him. [37] When Tàizǔ settled Jì Province, [Xiàhóu] Shàng became Army Major, commanded cavalry following on campaigns, later became Five Offices General’s Literary Scholar. When Wèi state was first established, promoted to Yellow Gate Attendant Cadet. Dài prefecture’s Hú rebelled, sent the Marquess of Yānlíng [Cáo] Zhāng to campaign and suppress them, with [Xiàhóu] Shàng as Advisor to [Cáo] Zhāng’s military affairs, settled Dài territory, returned. Tàizǔ passed away at Luòyáng, [Xiàhúo] Shàng Held Stave to serve the catalpa coffin in returning to Yè. Altogether noted former achievements, enfeoffed Marquess of Pínglíng precinct, appointed Cavalier Regular Attendant, promoted to Central Manager of the Army. When Emperor Wén ascended the throne, further enfeoffed as Marquess of Pínglíng village, promoted to Campaigning South General, designate Jīng Province Inspector, Lent Stave as Overall Supervisor of the south’s various military affairs. [Xiàhóu] Shàng memorialized: “Liú Bèi’s separate army is at Shàngyōng, the mountain roads rugged and difficult, they do not expect us, if we use surprise troops secretly traveling, setting out where they do not expect, then it is a situation for an independent success.” Therefore organized the various armies and struck and defeated Shàngyōng, pacified three prefectures and nine counties, promoted to Campaigning South General-in-Chief. Although Sūn Quán declared himself vassal, [Xiàhóu] Shàng increasingly prepared equipment for attacking and suppressing, [Sūn] Quán later indeed had duplicitous heart. Huángchū Third Year [222], the Chariot Carriage visited Wǎn, sent [Xiàhóu] Shàng to lead the various armies with Cáo Zhēn to together besiege Jiānglíng. [Sūn] Quán’s officer Zhūgě Jǐn with [Xiàhóu] Shàng’s army faced on the Jiāng, [Zhūgě] Jǐn crossed to enter an islet in the Jiāng, and divided a navy in the Jiāng. [Xiàhóu] Shàng in the night prepared main oiled ships,118 commanded infantry and cavalry of over ten thousand men, to the downstream secretly crossed, attacked [Zhūgě] Jǐn’s various armies, pinsered the Jiāng and burned their boats, water and land all attacking, defeated them. The city was not yet taken, it happened that a great epidemic, Edict ordered [Xiàhóu] Shàng to withdraw the various armies and return. Increased fief by six hundred households, adding with the previous to one thousand nine hundred households, Lent Battle-Ax, advanced to Governor. Jīng Province was ravaged and desolate, outside bordered Mán-Yí, and with Wú blocking the Hàn river as a border, of the old population many resided south of the Jiāng. [Xiàhóu] Shàng from Shàngyōng connected roads, west traveling over seven hundred lǐ, of the mountain peoples and Mán-Yí many submitted, within five to six years the surrendered and attached were several thosuand families. Fifth Year [224], relocated enfeoffment to Marquess of Chānglíng village. [Xiàhóu] Shàng had a beloved concubine favored with visits, favor taken away from the primary wife. The primary wife was the Cáo clan’s daughter, therefore Emperor Wén sent someone to strangle and kill her. [Xiàhóu] Shàng was sorrowful and emotional, fell ill and became dazed. After already burying the concubine, he could not bear his longing to see her, and again excavated her to see her. Emperor Wén heard and was enraged at him, and said: “Dù Xí’s disparagement of [Xiàhóu] Shàng had a good reason.” However as he was an old minster, the grace and favor did not decline. Sixth Year [225], [Xiàhóu] Shàng’s illness was critical, reeturned to the capital city, the Emperor repeatedly visited him, held his hand and shed tears. [Xiàhóu] Shàng died, posthumous name called Dào-hóu.119 [38] His son [Xiàhóu] Xuán succeeded. Also divided from [Xiàhóu] Shàng households of three hundred to bestow on [Xiàhóu] Shàng’s younger brother’s son [Xiàhóu] Fèng noble title as Marquess Within the Passes.



夏侯尚字伯仁，淵從子也。文帝與之親友。〔一〕太祖定冀州，尚為軍司馬，將騎從征伐，後為五官將文學。魏國初建，遷黃門侍郎。代郡胡叛，遣鄢陵侯彰征討之，以尚參彰軍事，定代地，還。太祖崩于洛陽，尚持節，奉梓宮還鄴。并錄前功，封平陵亭侯，拜散騎常侍，遷中領軍。文帝踐阼，更封平陵鄉侯，遷征南將軍，領荊州刺史，假節都督南方諸軍事。尚奏：「劉備別軍在上庸，山道險難，彼不我虞，若以奇兵潛行，出其不意，則獨克之勢也。」遂勒諸軍擊破上庸，平三郡九縣，遷征南大將軍。孫權雖稱藩，尚益脩攻討之備，權後果有貳心。黃初三年，車駕幸宛，使尚率諸軍與曹真共圍江陵。權將諸葛瑾與尚軍對江，瑾渡入江中渚，而分水軍于江中。尚夜多持油船，將步騎萬餘人，於下流潛渡，攻瑾諸軍，夾江燒其舟船，水陸並攻，破之。城未拔，會大疫，詔敕尚引諸軍還。益封六百戶，并前千九百戶，假鉞，進為牧。荊州殘荒，外接蠻夷，而與吳阻漢水為境，舊民多居江南。尚自上庸通道，西行七百餘里，山民蠻夷多服從者，五六年間，降附數千家。五年，徙封昌陵鄉侯。尚有愛妾嬖幸，寵奪適室；適室，曹氏女也，故文帝遣人絞殺之。尚悲感，發病恍惚，既葬埋妾，不勝思見，復出視之。文帝聞而恚之曰：「杜襲之輕薄尚，良有以也。」然以舊臣，恩寵不衰。六年，尚疾篤，還京都，帝數臨幸，執手涕泣。尚薨，諡曰悼侯。〔二〕子玄嗣。又分尚戶三百，賜尚弟子奉爵關內侯。










[37] Wèi shū states: [Xiàhóu] Shàng had strategic planning and tactical wisdom, Emperor Wén valued him, and they became friends in plain clothes.120



〔一〕　魏書曰：尚有籌畫智略，文帝器之，與為布衣之交。













[38] Wèi shū records the Edict stating: “[Xiàhóu] Shàng from youth attended and followed, thorough in sincerity and exhaustive in integrity, though he was said to be of a different surname, he was like my bone and flesh,121 therefore in entering he was my belly and heart, in exiting he was my claws and teeth. His tactical wisdom was deep and quick, his planning surpassed others, by misfortune he early died, such is fate, what can be done? Posthumously bequeath the Campaigning South General-in-Chief’s and Marquess of Chānglíng’s seals and ribbons.”



〔二〕　魏書載詔曰：「尚自少侍從，盡誠竭節，雖云異姓，其猶骨肉，是以入為腹心，出當爪牙。智略深敏，謀謨過人，不幸早殞，命也奈何！贈征南大將軍、昌陵侯印綬。」






Xiàhóu Xuán


[Xiàhóu] Xuán appellation Tàichū. In youth he was famed, on capping122 became Cavalier Yellow Gate Attendant Cadet. Once in advancing for a meeting, he was with the Imperial Empress’s younger brother Máo Zēng seated together. [Xiàhóu] Xuán was shamed by this, displeasuring showing in his expression. Emperor Míng resented this, demoted him to Feather Forest Overseer. At Zhèngshǐ’s beginning, Cáo Shuǎng assisted in government. [Xiàhóu] Xuán was [Cáo] Shuǎng’s father’s sister’s son. Gradually promoted to Cavalier Regular Attendant, Central Protector of the Army. [39]



玄字太初。少知名，弱冠為散騎黃門侍郎。嘗進見，與皇后弟毛曾並坐，玄恥之，不悅形之於色。明帝恨之，左遷為羽林監。正始初，曹爽輔政。玄，爽之姑子也。累遷散騎常侍、中護軍。〔一〕










[39] Shìyǔ states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán was famous for understanding men, became Central Protector of the Army, selecting and employing military offices, the advisors and guards and Ivory Gates,123 none were not outstanding talents, many became Governors of provinces and managers of prefectures. His established laws and bequeathed instructions to the present all were models for posterity.



〔一〕　世語曰：玄世名知人，為中護軍，拔用武官，參戟牙門，無非俊傑，多牧州典郡。立法垂教，于今皆為後式。







Grand Tutor Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng asked him about the time’s affairs, [Xiàhóu] Xuán commented believing: “The appointment of talents and employment of people, is the handle of the state. Therefore, evaluations and selections being concentrated at the Terrace Pavillion is the responsibility of the above; filial conduct maintained in the village alleys, merits and drawbacks assigned by village peoples, is the ordering of the below. The desire to purify instruction and investigate selections, is in making clear the responsibility and ordering, not allowing them to encroach on one another, and nothing more. Why is this? If the above overstep their responsibility, then one fears that their origins will not be from the roots, and so open the road to grasping at power and chasing influence. If the below exceed their ordering, then one fears that celestial titles will be connected with the exterior, and so the gates to critical power will be many. Celestial titles connecting with the below, is for common people to discuss the handles (of power). Critical power having many gates, is the origin of disorder and chaos. Since the coming of provincial and prefectural Central Rectifiers ranking and grading the appointments of talents, it has been for many years, remaining disordered, never hearing of organization, how is this not due to responsibility and ordering becoming intermingled, each losing their essentials? If it is ordered that Central Rectifiers only examine conduct by class of peers, the standard of conduct for a class of peers being matched, this can be appointed. Why is this? If filial conduct is proven in the family gates, how can they not be loyal and scrupulous in their appointments? If benevolence and forbearance is praised in the nine clans, how can they not be understanding in enacting government? If righteous decisiceness is enacted in the home community, how can they not be able to bear tasks and assignments? These three categories, selected by the Central Rectifiers, even if they do not place them in appointed office, the fitness for appointment can be known. Conduct has large and small, comparisons have high and low, then the categories of appointments, also naturally become clearly differentiated. Why must one have the Central Rectifiers interfere in the mechanisms of evaluations and selections at the below, and so have those grasping the mechanisms and handles have to delegate authority from above, above and below infringing on one another, and so creating disordered intermingling? Moreover the Terrace Pavillions oversee the below, examining achievements and inspecting wrongs, the associates of the numerous duties, each have their office chiefs, dawn to dusk examining one another, nothing investigates as thoroughly as this. The discussions of the village alleys, are determined by opinions, and so if it causes skilled administrators to lose positions, everyone becomes agitated and alarmed. The desire for social customs to be purified and tranquil, how could it be obtained? The Celestial Terrace hangs far away, cut off from the opinions of the masses. Those able to arrive, further are close nearby, who would not craft embellishments to obtain what they seek? Once there is a road to what they seek, then those that cultivated themselves in their family gates, already cannot compare to those who advanced themselves in their local communities, and those that advanced themselves in their local communities, already cannot compare to those that themselves sought it from the provincial authorities. If one opens that road, and yet worries that the embellishment of the true will depart from the roots, even if one further strictly reproached the Central Rectifiers, disciplining them with punishments, yet it would be without benefit. How would it compare to having each command their responsibility, the office chiefs then would each by the capability or inability of their associates proffer them to the Terrace Pavillions, the Terrace Pavillions then would act in accordance to the rankings of the capability or inability of the office chiefs, supplemented with the gradings of virtue and conduct in local communities, assessed in comparison to peers, without allowing partiality or bias. Central Rectifiers then would only examine the conduct and legacies, differentiating the high and low, judging and determining categories, without allowing promotion or demotion. The Terrace Pavillions would control it, in accordance with their selections. If there are mistakes, then the responsibility naturally is on the relevant managers. The rankings by the office chiefs, the categorizations by Central Rectifiers, compare and in accordance to established grading then employ them, and if they are not suitable, the responsibility is on the exterior. That being the case, interior and exterior consult with one another, successes and failures have their attributions, each exposing and inspecting one another, who would be able to embellish one another? Then the people’s hearts are settled and affairs are managed and completed, and perhaps we may tranquilize social custom and examine the appointment of talents.”
He also believed: “The ancients established offices in order to aid and nurture the various living, preside and administer the people. Therefore they appointed lords and chiefs to manage and herd them. The principle of managing and herding, is a wish to unify and concentrate. If unified then office responsibilities are settled and so above and below are secure. If concentrated then duties are performed and so affairs are not cumbersome. When affairs are simple and duties performed, a case of above and below both secure and yet not governed, has never been. The Former Kings established myriad states, although the details cannot be recovered and thoroughly investigated, however they divided borders and drew boundaries, each guarding their territory, then this was not a system of overlapping restraints. Down to investigate the orderings of the Five Ranks of Yīn and Zhōu, it only had the differentiation of small and large and noble and lowly, and also had no lords and officials and servants and people yet having two chains of command restraining one another. If the official chain of command is not unified, then duties are not performed. If duties are not performed, then how can matters be kept simple? If matters are not simple, then how can the people be kept tranquil? If the people are not tranquil, then wrongdoing and evil together arise, and so treachery and fraud grow and expand. The Former Kings understood it would be like this, and therefore concentrated the duties of management and unified the chain of command. Beginning from Qín’s era, they did not take as teacher the sagely ways, used self-interest in managing duties, used treachery in treating subordinates. Fearing the governing officials would not perform, they established overseers to supervise them, and fearing the overseers would tolerate wrongdoing, they established inspectors to investigate them. Governors and supervisors entangled one another, overseers and inspectors managed one another, the people harbored divergent hearts, above and below separated in functions. Hàn continued these threads, none able to rectify and reform it. In the expansion of the Wèi House, the days did not have the leisure to attend to it. The institutions of the Five Ranks, although difficult to suddenly restore, can be roughly established in ceremony and standards in order to unify the government system. The present chief clerks all govern the clerks and people, with another layer of the prefecture Administrators, added again with the Inspectors. If the jurisdiction of the prefecture is only in overall scope, then it is the same as with the province, and no reason for a duplication. It is appropriate to abolish the prefecture Administrator, and only appoint Inspectors. If the Inspector duty is kept then supervision is not abandoned. The prefectural clerks numbering in the tens of thousands will return to personally farming, thus reducing complexity and costs, increasing wealth and growing grain. This is first. The talents of large counties all can be prefecture administrators. Disputes over right or wrong always create differing opinions. To comply then is peace, to maintain oneself then is conflict. The beauty of harmonious stew is in uniting the different, the advantage of above and below is in the ability to complement one another. Compliance for peace, this is the zither and zithern playing one note.124 To sweep away and eliminate this, then offices are reduced and matters are simplified. This is second. Also the clerks of administering prefectures, their duty is to oversee the various counties, they strive to protect their faction and kin, local connections and old associates, if any do not submit, then they take advantage of public affairs to harass and obstruct. The destitution and distress of the people arises from this. If they were all merged and combined, then the source of the chaos would naturally be blocked. This is third. Now having inherited decline and damage, the people are diminished and depleted, worthy talents are rare and few, those appointed to affairs are scarce. The good clerks of prefectures and counties, generally are not only one, the prefectures receive what counties complete, thus the demanding work is below, but in the selecting above of clerks, the prefectures are the first supplied, this is to make the clerks closest to the people to be concentrated with the lowest caliber. The clerks determine the lives of the people, but yet are often stubborn and crude. Now if merging them, more clerks selected as pure and good will fill these duties, great cultivation will spread and flow, the people will attain peace. This is fourth. Systemize by having counties of ten thousand households be called as prefecture Administrators, five thousand and above called as Commandants, thousand households and below, Magistrates and Chiefs as before. From Chief and above, examine and test for promotion and employment, transfer and by ability rise, and those they govern will also increase, this is an ordering for advancing talent and rewarding achievement. If the core system is unified and settled, then appointment of talents has sequencing, and the achievements of governing will be uniform and clear. This is fifth. If the prefecture Administrators are abolished, the counties all directly connected, matters are not obstructed and partitioned, offices are without delay, and although the airs of the Three Dynasties cannot yet be guaranteed, the transformation of simplicity and unity, perhaps can be delivered. Conveniencing the people and reducing costs is in this.”
He also believed: “Refinement and substance alternate in use, like the four seasons in succession rise. A King that embodies Heaven and orders people, must in response to detriments then relieve and resolve them, in seasons of excessive substance then refine them with rituals, in seasons of extreme extravagance then rescue them with substance. Now in inheriting the end of the Hundred Kings, the lingering flows of Qín and Hàn, the worldy customs are excessively refined, it is appropriate to greatly reform them to change the people’s expectations. In present laws and regulations, from Dukes and Ranked Marquesses on down and positions from General-in-Chief and above, all are able to wear damask brocade, patterned silks, delicate white silks, objects of gold and silver ornaments and engravings, from this on down, clothes of mixed colors are available through to the lowly people. Although above and below ranks and grades each show their differentiations, however the systems of the Court ministers already are able to compare to the Utmost Honored, the colors of dark and yellow are already available through to subordinates. A desire to have the market not sell flowery and gorgeous colors, merchants not trade difficult to obtain goods, crafters not make engraved objects, cannot be obtained. Therefore it is appropriate to greatly manage the roots, standardize and limit by ancient laws, by the appropriateness of refinement and substance take the middle standards, to be ritual norms. Chariot carriages and clothing insignia, all are to follow substance and simplicity, prohibit and eliminate the flowery and gorgeous matters of end point customs, cause the families of those serving at Court and the households of those with positions to no longer have ornaments of brocade and patterned silk, be without clothing of multiple colors, and objects of delicate intricacies. From the above on down, reach to differentiation of plainness and simplicity, to show the ranks and grades and nothing more, and not allow it to exceed one to two distinctions. As for bestowments for achievements and virtues, and what the Superior’s grace specially applies, all are to be registered by relevant managers, and only afterward worn and used. The above influencing the below, is like the wind bending grass. If the teachings of plain simplicity rise in the current Court, then the heart of excessive extravagance will on its own vanish below.”



太傅司馬宣王問以時事，玄議以為：「夫官才用人，國之柄也，故銓衡專於臺閣，上之分也，孝行存乎閭巷，優劣任之鄉人，下之敘也。夫欲清教審選，在明其分敘，不使相涉而已。何者？上過其分，則恐所由之不本，而干勢馳騖之路開；下踰其敘，則恐天爵之外通，而機權之門多矣。夫天爵下通，是庶人議柄也；機權多門，是紛亂之原也。自州郡中正品度官才之來，有年載矣，緬緬紛紛，未聞整齊，豈非分敘參錯，各失其要之所由哉！若令中正但考行倫輩，倫輩當行均，斯可官矣。何者？夫孝行著於家門，豈不忠恪於在官乎？仁恕稱於九族，豈不達於為政乎？義斷行於鄉黨，豈不堪於事任乎？三者之類，取於中正，雖不處其官名，斯任官可知矣。行有大小，比有高下，則所任之流，亦渙然明別矣。奚必使中正干銓衡之機於下，而執機柄者有所委仗於上，上下交侵，以生紛錯哉？且臺閣臨下，考功校否，眾職之屬，各有官長，旦夕相考，莫究於此；閭閻之議，以意裁處，而使匠宰失位，眾人驅駭，欲風俗清靜，其可得乎？天臺縣遠，眾所絕意。所得至者，更在側近，孰不脩飾以要所求？所求有路，則脩己家門者，已不如自達于鄉黨矣。自達鄉黨者，已不如自求之於州邦矣。苟開之有路，而患其飾真離本，雖復嚴責中正，督以刑罰，猶無益也。豈若使各帥其分，官長則各以其屬能否獻之臺閣，臺閣則據官長能否之第，參以鄉閭德行之次，擬其倫比，勿使偏頗。中正則唯考其行跡，別其高下，審定輩類，勿使升降。臺閣總之，如其所簡，或有參錯，則其責負自在有司。官長所第，中正輩擬，比隨次率而用之，如其不稱，責負在外。然則內外相參，得失有所，互相形檢，孰能相飾？斯則人心定而事理得，庶可以靜風俗而審官才矣。」又以為：「古之建官，所以濟育群生，統理民物也，故為之君長以司牧之。司牧之主，欲一而專，一則官任定而上下安，專則職業脩而事不煩。夫事簡業脩，上下相安而不治者，未之有也。先王建萬國，雖其詳未可得而究，然分疆畫界，各守土境，則非重累羈絆之體也。下考殷、周五等之敘，徒有小大貴賤之差，亦無君官臣民而有二統互相牽制者也。夫官統不一，則職業不脩；職業不脩，則事何得而簡？事之不簡，則民何得而靜？民之不靜，則邪惡並興，而姦偽滋長矣。先王達其如此，故專其職司而一其統業。始自秦世，不師聖道，私以御職，姦以待下；懼宰官之不脩，立監牧以董之，畏督監之容曲，設司察以糾之；宰牧相累，監察相司，人懷異心，上下殊務。漢承其緒，莫能匡改。魏室之隆，日不暇及，五等之典，雖難卒復，可麤立儀準以一治制。今之長吏，皆君吏民，橫重以郡守，累以刺史。若郡所攝，唯在大較，則與州同，無為再重。宜省郡守，但任刺史；刺史職存則監察不廢，郡吏萬數，還親農業，以省煩費，豐財殖穀，一也。大縣之才，皆堪郡守，是非之訟，每生意異，順從則安，直己則爭。夫和羹之美，在於合異，上下之益，在能相濟，順從乃安，此琴瑟一聲也，蕩而除之，則官省事簡，二也。又幹郡之吏，職監諸縣，營護黨親，鄉邑舊故，如有不副，而因公掣頓，民之困弊，咎生于此，若皆并合，則亂原自塞，三也。今承衰弊，民人彫莈，賢才鮮少，任事者寡，郡縣良吏，往往非一，郡受縣成，其劇在下，而吏之上選，郡當先足，此為親民之吏，專得底下，吏者民命，而常頑鄙，今如并之，吏多選清良者造職，大化宣流，民物獲寧，四也。制使萬戶之縣，名之郡守，五千以上，名之都尉，千戶以下，令長如故，自長以上，考課遷用，轉以能升，所牧亦增，此進才效功之敘也，若經制一定，則官才有次，治功齊明，五也。若省郡守，縣皆徑達，事不擁隔，官無留滯，三代之風，雖未可必，簡一之化，庶幾可致，便民省費，在於此矣。」又以為：「文質之更用，猶四時之迭興也，王者體天理物，必因弊而濟通之，時彌質則文之以禮，時泰侈則救之以質。今承百王之末，秦漢餘流，世俗彌文，宜大改之以易民望。今科制自公、列侯以下，位從大將軍以上，皆得服綾錦、羅綺、紈素、金銀飾鏤之物，自是以下，雜綵之服，通于賤人，雖上下等級，各示有差，然朝臣之制，已得侔至尊矣，玄黃之采，已得通於下矣。欲使市不鬻華麗之色，商不通難得之貨，工不作彫刻之物，不可得也。是故宜大理其本，準度古法，文質之宜，取其中則，以為禮度。車輿服章，皆從質樸，禁除末俗華麗之事，使幹朝之家，有位之室，不復有錦綺之飾，無兼采之服，纖巧之物，自上以下，至于樸素之差，示有等級而已，勿使過一二之覺。若夫功德之賜，上恩所特加，皆表之有司，然後服用之。夫上之化下，猶風之靡草。樸素之教興於本朝，則彌侈之心自消於下矣。」




[Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng’s reply letter said: “Scrutinizing offices and selecting men, eliminating redundant offices, reforming clothing regulations, all are very good. Respecting local community root conduct, the Court examining matters, the main point is as you indicated. But in the interim’s it all became successively maintained habits, in the end it cannot be reformed. In Qín’s time there were no Inspectors, only having Prefecture Administrators and Chief Clerks. Although the Hàn House had Inspectors, they observed Six Statutes and nothing more, and therefore Inspectors were called as Transfer Chariots, their clerks were called Following Officials, their residences had no regular headquarters, their clerks did not become complete servants, only from then afterward they transformed further into official managers. In the past Jiǎ Yì also worried over clothing regulations, although Hàn Wén’s personal clothing was coarse silk, yet he was not able to cause above and below to be as he wished. One fears that these three matters must wait for the worthy and capable and only afterward be resolved.”
[Xiàhóu] Xuán also wrote letter that said: “Although Hàn Wén personally wore coarse silk, yet he did not reform and correct the law institutions, the interior and exterior had clothing of usurpative imitation, favored servants received bestowals without limits, by this observing him, it seems his direction was to establish a reputation for himself, it was not an intention to sincerely standardize and govern regulations. Now Your Excellency Marquess has been mandated by the world to be the highest minister, follows the footsteps of high antiquity, seeking to expand to utmost governance, restrict tips and correct the roots, if the regulations are settled at the top, then transformation spreads to the multitudes. When facing a time appropriate for reform, one should keep an eagerly diligent heart. On the day the order is issued, the answer of those below is like merely an echo following a sound. Yet you hold to excessive modesty, stating: ‘Wait for the worthy and capable,’ this is Yī and Zhōu not correcting the standards of Yīn and Jī.125 I humbly do not understand it.”
