宣王報書曰：「審官擇人，除重官，改服制，皆大善。禮鄉閭本行，朝廷考事，大指如所示。而中間一相承習，卒不能改。秦時無刺史，但有郡守長吏。漢家雖有刺史，奉六條而已，故刺史稱傳車，其吏言從事，居無常治，吏不成臣，其後轉更為官司耳。昔賈誼亦患服制，漢文雖身服弋綈，猶不能使上下如意。恐此三事，當待賢能然後了耳。」玄又書曰：「漢文雖身衣弋綈，而不革正法度，內外有僭擬之服，寵臣受無限之賜，由是觀之，似指立在身之名，非篤齊治制之意也。今公侯命世作宰，追蹤上古，將隆至治，抑末正本，若制定於上，則化行於眾矣。夫當宜改之時，留殷勤之心，令發之日，下之應也猶響尋聲耳，猶垂謙謙，曰『待賢能』，此伊周不正殷姬之典也。竊未喻焉。」




Shortly after this, he became Campaigning West General, Lent Stave as Overall Supervisor of Yōng and Liáng Provinces’ various military affairs. [40] With Cáo Shuǎng they together raised the Luò valley campaign, at the time people ridiculed him. When [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed, summoned [Xiàhóu] Xuán to be Minister Herald, in a few years transferred to Minister of Ceremonies. [Xiàhóu] Xuán, because of [Cáo] Shuǎng was restrained and dismissed, inside he was not content. Central Writers Director Lǐ Fēng although formerly had been by General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng closely treated, however his private heart was with [Xiàhóu] Xuán, and therefore he joined the Imperial Empress’s father the Radiant Grandee Zhāng Qī to plot a wish to have [Xiàhóu] Xuán assist the government. [Lǐ] Fēng already inside held the handles of power, his son was bestowed a princess, and also he and [Zhāng] Qī both were Féngyì men, therefore [Zhāng] Qī trusted him. [Lǐ] Fēng secretly ordered his younger brother the Yǎn Province Inspector [Lǐ] Yì to request to enter Court, wishing to have him lead troops to enter, and combine strength to rise up. It happened that [Lǐ] Yì’s request to attend Court was not permitted. Jiāpíng Sixth Year Second Moon [254 Mar 6 - Apr 4], there was to be an appointment of a Noble Lady, [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest wished to take advantage of the Imperial oversight of the pavillions, the various gates having ramp troops,126 to execute the General-in-Chief, with [Xiàhóu] Xuán succeeding him, and with [Zhāng] Qī as Agile Cavalry General. [Lǐ] Fēng secretly spoke with Yellow Gate Overseer Sū Shuò, Yǒngníng Bureau Director Yuè Dūn, and Surplus Follower Deputy Director Liú Xián and others stating: “You sirs reside in the interior, have made many violations of the law, the General-in-Chief is strict and stern, and repeatedly spoken about this. Zhāng Dāng can be a warning.” [Sū] Shuò and the rest all agreed to follow orders. [41] The General-in-Chief slightly heard of this plot, invited [Lǐ] Fēng to a meeting, [Lǐ] Fēng was unaware and went, at once killed him. [42] The matter was sent down to the relevant managers, arrested [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Zhāng] Qī, [Sū] Shuò, [Yuè] Dūn, [Liú] Xián and the rest and sent to the Minister of Justice. [43] Minister of Justice Zhōng Yù memorialized: “[Lǐ] Fēng and the rest plotted to coerce the Utmost Honored, usurp authority to execute the most senior minister, Great Rebellion Without Morality, request to discuss it following the law.” Thereupon gathered the Excellencies and Ministers and Court councilors and Minister of Justice to discuss, all believed: “[Lǐ] Fēng and the rest each receved exceptional favor, managed and administered the critical and confidential, [Zhāng] Qī held the honor of the in-law relation pepper rooms,127 [Xiàhóu] Xuán served as a generational minister, both residing in ranked positions, but secretly hid disastrous hearts, plotting vicious rebellion, consorting with castrate eunuchs, entrusting them with treasonous plans, in fear of heavenly authority, not daring to openly plot, instead wishing to coerce lord and threaten superior, indulging in their deceit and cruelty, plotting to execute the good assistant, usurp authority to establish one another, about to overturn the capital house, topple and endanger the State Altars. What [Zhōng] Yù has standardized is all in accordance to law, reply to [Zhōng] Yù to put it into effect.” Edict said: “The Senior Princess of Qí is the Former Emperor’s beloved legacy, pardon her three children from death.” Thereupon [Lǐ] Fēng, [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Zhāng] Qī, [Yuè] Dūn, [Liú] Xián and others were all exterminated three clans, [44] the remaining kin and dependents were exiled to Lèlàng prefecture. [Xiàhóu] Xuán in bearing was tolerant and magnanimous, facing execution in the East Market, his expression did not change, his movements were at ease, at the time aged forty-six. [45] During Zhèngyuán [254 - 255], to continue the successions of accomplished ministers, enfeoffed [Xiàhóu] Shàng’s cousin’s grandson [Xiàhóu] Běn as Marquess of Chānglíng precinct, estate three hundred households, to serve as [Xiàhóu] Shàng’s posterity.



頃之，為征西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。〔一〕與曹爽共興駱谷之役，時人譏之。爽誅，徵玄為大鴻臚，數年徙太常。玄以爽抑絀，內不得意。中書令李豐雖宿為大將軍司馬景王所親待，然私心在玄，遂結皇后父光祿大夫張緝，謀欲以玄輔政。豐既內握權柄，子尚公主，又與緝俱馮翊人，故緝信之。豐陰令弟兗州刺史翼求入朝，欲使將兵入，并力起。會翼求朝，不聽。嘉平六年二月，當拜貴人，豐等欲因御臨軒，諸門有陛兵，誅大將軍，以玄代之，以緝為驃騎將軍。豐密語黃門監蘇鑠、永寧署令樂敦、宂從僕射劉賢等曰：「卿諸人居內，多有不法，大將軍嚴毅，累以為言，張當可以為誡。」鑠等皆許以從命。〔二〕大將軍微聞其謀，請豐相見，豐不知而往，即殺之。〔三〕事下有司，收玄、緝、鑠、敦、賢等送廷尉。〔四〕廷尉鍾毓奏：「豐等謀迫脅至尊，擅誅冢宰，大逆無道，請論如法。」於是會公卿朝臣廷尉議，咸以為「豐等各受殊寵，典綜機密，緝承外戚椒房之尊，玄備世臣，並居列位，而包藏禍心，搆圖凶逆，交關閹豎，授以姦計，畏憚天威，不敢顯謀，乃欲要君脅上，肆其詐虐，謀誅良輔，擅相建立，將以傾覆京室，顛危社稷。毓所正皆如科律，報毓施行」。詔書：「齊長公主，先帝遺愛，原其三子死命。」於是豐、玄、緝、敦、賢等皆夷三族，〔五〕其餘親屬徙樂浪郡。玄格量弘濟，臨斬東巿，顏色不變，舉動自若，時年四十六。〔六〕正元中，紹功臣世，封尚從孫本為昌陵亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉尚後。










[40] Wèi lüè states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán had been promoted, Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng succeeded him as Protector of the Army. Protector of the Army presided over the various officers, appointed to manage military office selections and nominations, beginning to end those that had held this office had been unable to stop bribery. Therefore at the time when Jiǎng Jì was Protector of the Army, there was a folk song: “Wishing to seek Ivory Gate, one must have a thousand pǐ; a hundred men supervisor, five hundred pǐ.”128 [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng and [Jiǎng] Jì were friends, he privately asked [Jiǎng] Jì about it, [Jiǎng] Jì had no way to explain it, and therefore jokingly said: “In Luò’s central market purchases, if a single coin is lacking then it is not enacted.” Therefore facing one another they laughed. [Xiàhóu] Xuán succeeded [Jiǎng] Jì, and therefore was not able to stop and cut off human affairs. Reaching to [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng succeeding [Xiàhóu] Xuán, he organized laws and decrees, of people none violated.



〔一〕　魏略曰：玄既遷，司馬景王代為護軍。護軍總統諸將，任主武官選舉，前後當此官者，不能止貨賂。故蔣濟為護軍時，有謠言「欲求牙門，當得千匹；百人督，五百匹」。宣王與濟善，閒以問濟，濟無以解之，因戲曰：「洛中市買，一錢不足則不行。」遂相對歡笑。玄代濟，故不能止絕人事。及景王之代玄，整頓法令，人莫犯者。













[41] Wèi shū states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán had formerly been noble, due to [Cáo] Shuǎng was deposed and dismissed, resided ever in resentment and discontent. Central Writers Director Lǐ Fēng with [Xiàhóu] Xuán and the Empress’s father Radiant Grandee Zhāng Qī secretly plotted to make chaos, [Zhāng] Qī with [Lǐ] Fēng were of the same prefecture and was a cunning crafty man, from Dōngguǎn Administrator had been summoned due to being of the Empress’ family, also was discontent, and therefore they all together plotted. Previously, [Lǐ] Fēng himself believed he personally occupied the critical and confidential, his son [Lǐ] Tāo also as a Ranked Marquess was Dispensing Affairs Central, bestowed the Senior Princess of Qí, having value inside and outside, his heart could not be at ease. Secretly he spoke with [Lǐ] Tāo stating: “[Xiàhóu] Xuán already is a valued man Within the Seas, and additionally should have great responsibilities, his age is at his prime yet he forever meets with abandonment, and also is Cáo Shuǎng’s maternal younger cousin, with the General-in-Chief having enmities. I have obtained [Xiàhóu] Xuán’s letters, and deeply worry about this. [Zhāng] Qī has talent and ability, relinquished troops and horses in a large prefecture, returning to sit idly at home. Each do not obtain their ambitions, I wish to send you to inform them of the secret plans.” [Zhāng] Qī once was ill and bedridden, [Lǐ] Fēng sent [Lǐ] Tāo to check on his illness, [Lǐ] Tāo dismissed the others and spoke with [Zhāng] Qī stating: “[I, Lǐ] Tāo was bestowed a princess, father and son are in the critical close, the General-in-Chief controls affairs, we always fear to not meet with understanding and trust, the Minister of Ceremonies also feels deep anxiety. Although you Lord Marquess have the honor of being the Empress’s father, security and danger cannot yet be known, you have all the same concerns as [my, Lǐ] Tāo’s family. [My, Lǐ] Tāo’s father wishes to with you Lord Marquess plan about this.” [Zhāng] Qī was silent for a long time and said: “In the difficulties of sharing a boat, where can I flee? This is a great affair, to not succeed is for disaster to reach the entire clan.” [Lǐ] Tāo thereupon went to report to [Lǐ] Fēng. Secretly speaking with Yellow Gate Overseer Sū Shuò and others, Sū Shuò and the others answered to [Lǐ] Fēng: “We will follow the Lord Marquess’s plans.” [Lǐ] Fēng spoke stating: “Now in the appointment of a Noble Lady, the various camp troops all garrison the gates. His Majesty will oversee the pavilion, taking advantage of this to then together surround him, we will lead the various offices of men and troops, to then execute the General-in-Chief. You all will together secretly inform him of this intention.” [Sū] Shuò and the other said: “If His Majesty perhaps does not follow, what then?” [Lǐ] Fēng said: “Affairs have their expediences. At the time if he does not trust and listen, then merely take him away. How can he not follow?” [Sū] Shuò and the rest agreed. [Lǐ] Fēng said: “This is a matter of clan exterminations, you all keep it confidential. If the matter succeeds, you all will be enfeoffed as Marquesses and Regular Attendants.” [Lǐ] Fēng again secretly informed [Xiàhóu] Xuán and [Zhāng] Qī. [Zhāng] Qī sent his son [Zhāng] Miǎo to with [Lǐ] Fēng join with one another and together plot the uprising affairs.
Shìyǔ states: [Lǐ] Fēng sent his son [Lǐ] Tāo to report the plan to [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán said: “It should be considered in detail,” but did not report it.



〔二〕　魏書曰：玄素貴，以爽故廢黜，居常怏怏不得意。中書令李豐與玄及后父光祿大夫張緝陰謀為亂，緝與豐同郡，傾巧人也，以東莞太守召，為后家，亦不得意，故皆同謀。初，豐自以身處機密，息韜又以列侯給事中，尚齊長公主，有內外之重，心不自安。密謂韜曰：「玄既為海內重人，加以當大任，年時方壯而永見廢，又親曹爽外弟，於大將軍有嫌。吾得玄書，深以為憂。緝有才用，棄兵馬大郡，還坐家巷。各不得志，欲使汝以密計告之。」緝嘗病創臥，豐遣韜省病，韜屏人語緝曰：「韜尚公主，父子在機近，大將軍秉事，常恐不見明信，太常亦懷深憂。君侯雖有后父之尊，安危未可知，皆與韜家同慮者也，韜父欲與君侯謀之。」緝默然良久曰：「同舟之難，吾焉所逃？此大事，不捷即禍及宗族。」韜於是往報豐。密語黃門監蘇鑠等，蘇鑠等答豐：「惟君侯計。」豐言曰：「今拜貴人，諸營兵皆屯門。陛下臨軒，因此便共迫脅，將群寮人兵，就誅大將軍。卿等當共密白此意。」鑠等曰；「陛下儻不從人，奈何？」豐等曰：「事有權宜，臨時若不信聽，便當劫將去耳。那得不從？」鑠等許諾。豐曰：「此族滅事，卿等密之。事成，卿等皆當封侯常侍也。」豐復密以告玄、緝。緝遣子邈與豐相結，同謀起事。世語曰：豐遣子韜以謀報玄，玄曰「宜詳之耳」，而不以告也。













[42] Shìyǔ states: The General-in-Chief heard of [Lǐ] Fēng’s plot, Resident Wáng Yàng requested for orders to invite [Lǐ] Fēng: “If [Lǐ] Fēng is without preparations, his circumstance constrained and situation pressured, he will certainly come. If he does not come, [I, Wáng] Yàng one man alone am sufficient to restrain him. If he knows the plot has leaked, he will with multitudes clasp wields, long halberds defend himself, directly enter Yúnlóng Gate, seize Heaven’s Son and ascend Língyún Terrace. Atop the terrace are three thousand men with weapons, trumpeting and drumming to gather multitudes. If it comes to this, [I, Wáng] Yàng cannot reach him.” The General-in-Chief thus sent [Wáng] Yàng with a chariot to invite him. [Lǐ] Fēng was coerced and pressured, accompanied [Wáng] Yàng and arrived.
Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: The General-in-Chief rebuked [Lǐ] Fēng. [Lǐ] Fēng knew disaster had arrived, and therefore with stern expression said: “You and your father harbor treachery, about to overturn the State Altars. I only regret that my strength is inferior, unable to capture and extermiante you!” The General-in-Chief was furious, and had strong warriors with a saber pommel strike [Lǐ] Fēng’s waist, killing him.
Wèi lüè states: [Lǐ] Fēng appellation Ānguó was former Minister of the Guard Lǐ Yì’s son. During Huángchū, due to his father’s appointment he was summoned to accompany the army. Beginning in the time he was in plain clothes, aged seventeen to eighteen, around Yè he was famed for purity, for understanding and evaluating people, Within the Seas was in agreement, none not taking note of him. Later he accompanied the army and was at Xǔchāng, his acclaim daily expanded. His father did not agree with this, and therefore ordered to shut the gates, commanding to have him cut off from guests. Previously, when Emperor Míng was at the East Palace, [Lǐ] Fēng was among his Literary Scholars. Reaching to succeeding the Honored Throne, he obtained a Wú surrendered man, and asked: “Who are the famed servicemen of the Central States that are heard of east of the Jiāng?” The surrendered man said: “We have heard of a Lǐ Ānguó.” At the time [Lǐ] Fēng was a Yellow Gate Cadet, Emperor Míng asked his Left and Right where [Lǐ] Ānguó was, the Left and Right replied with [Lǐ] Fēng. The Emperor said: “Has [Lǐ] Fēng’s fame thus spread to Wú and Yuè?” Later transferred to Cavalry Commandant, Dispensing Affairs Central. After the Emperor passed away, became Yǒngníng Minsiter Charioteer. As his fame surpassed the truth, his ability to be employed was little. During Zhèngshǐ [240 - 249], promoted to Attendant Central Secretariat Writers Deputy Director. [Lǐ] Fēng at the Terrace Offices always often claimed illness. At the time Terrace Regulations was that when illness filled a hundred days one would lose salary. When [Lǐ] Fēng’s illness had not yet filled several tens of days, at once he would temporarily rise, and then return to bed, and it was like this for several years. Prevoiusly, [Lǐ] Fēng’s son [Lǐ] Tāo was selected to be bestowed a princess, [Lǐ] Fēng although outside declined it, inside he was not very apprehensive. [Lǐ] Fēng’s younger brothers [Lǐ] Yì and [Lǐ] Wěi served for several years, both successively as prefecture Administrators. [Lǐ] Fēng once among other people prominently admonished his two younger brothers, saying they should use their honored positions for [missing character]. Reaching to when Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng was ill for a long time, [Lǐ] Wěi was a Two Thousand dàn, indulged in alcohol, disordering Xīnpíng and Fúfēng two prefectures, but [Lǐ] Fēng did not summon him, everyone believed it relying on favor. When Cáo Shuǎng controlled the government, [Lǐ] Fēng vacillated between the two Excellencies, without having a definite side, therefore at the time there was a slanderous letter that said: “Cáo Shuǎng’s power is hot like soup, the Grand Tutor father and sons cold like paste, Lǐ Fēng and his brothers like wandering lights.” Its meaning was that although [Lǐ] Fēng outside showed purity and tranquility, yet inside plotted affairs, having similarity to wandering lights.129 Reaching to when [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng memorialized to execute [Cáo] Shuǎng, he stopped his chariot below the watchtowers, with [Lǐ] Fēng exchanging news, [Lǐ] Fēng was terrified, suddenly his breath stopped, his legs fell limp to the ground, unable to rise. Reaching Jiāpíng Fourth Year after [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng had died, the Central Writers Director position was vacant, the General-in-Chief [Sīmǎ Shī] consulted and asked the Court councilors: “Who can fill it?” Someone pointed toward [Lǐ] Fēng. Although [Lǐ] Fēng knew this was not a prestigious selection, yet himself believed he was joined by marriage with the country, thought to attach to the Utmost Honored, and therefore prostrated without declining, therefore memorialized to employ him. [Lǐ] Fēng was the Central Writers for two years, the Emperor almost always alone summoned and spoke with him, it was unknown what was said. [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng knew they were discussing him, invited [Lǐ] Fēng, [Lǐ] Fēng would not report the truth, thus killed him. The affair was kept secret. [Lǐ] Fēng beginning to end served successively Two Courts, did not give attention to household finances, relying on his salary and grain stipend and nothing more. Although [Lǐ] Tāo was bestowed a princess, [Lǐ] Fēng always restricted and warned him to not infringe or take anything. At times obtaining bestowals of cash and silk, at once he outside distributed it to kin and clan. When there were bestowals of Palace women, most gave them to junior relatives, but [Lǐ] Fēng all gave them to his various sister’s sons. Reaching to after he died, relevant managers audited his household, the household was without remaining accumulations.
Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: In the night sent [Lǐ] Fēng’s corpse to give over the Minister of Justice. Minister of Justice Zhōng Yù would not accept, stating: “This is not what the law office manages.” He was informed of the situation, and moreover commanded to, and so accepted it. The Emperor was angry, about to investigate the circumstances of [Lǐ] Fēng’s death. The Dowager Empress was afraid, called the Emperor inside, and so it stopped. Sent envoy to arrest [Lǐ] Yì.
Shìyǔ states: [Lǐ] Yì’s later wife was Cavalier Regular Attendant Xún Yì’s older sister, spoke to [Lǐ] Yì stating: “The Central Writers affair is discovered, you can when the letters have not yet arrived flee to Wú, why sit and wait for death? Of your Left and Right who can with you together go through water and fire?” [Lǐ] Yì thought and could not answer, his wife said: “You governed a large province, do not know anyone who can with you share in death or life, to flee also is to not escape.” [Lǐ] Yì said: “My two sons are small. I will not flee. Now I am only implicated by connection, I will die, but the two sons will certainly be spared.” Indeed it was as [Lǐ] Yì said. [Lǐ] Yì’s son [Lǐ] Bīn was Yáng Jùn’s sister’s son. At Jìn Emperor Huì’s beginning, he became Hénán Intendant, with [Yáng] Jùn together died, see Jìn shū.



〔三〕　世語曰：大將軍聞豐謀，舍人王羕請以命請豐。「豐若無備，情屈勢迫，必來，若不來，羕一人足以制之；若知謀泄，以眾挾輪，長戟自衛，徑入雲龍門，挾天子登淩雲臺，臺上有三千人仗，鳴鼓會眾，如此，羕所不及也」。大將軍乃遣羕以車迎之。豐見劫迫，隨羕而至。魏氏春秋曰：大將軍責豐，豐知禍及，遂正色曰：「卿父子懷姦，將傾社稷，惜吾力劣，不能相禽滅耳！」大將軍怒，使勇士以刀環築豐腰，殺之。魏略曰：豐字安國，故衛尉李義子也。黃初中，以父任召隨軍。始為白衣時，年十七八，在鄴下名為清白，識別人物，海內翕然，莫不注意。後隨軍在許昌，聲稱日隆。其父不願其然，遂令閉門，敕使斷客。初，明帝在東宮，豐在文學中。及即尊位，得吳降人，問「江東聞中國名士為誰」？降人云：「聞有李安國者是。」時豐為黃門郎，明帝問左右安國所在，左右以豐對。帝曰：「豐名乃被于吳越邪？」後轉騎都尉、給事中。帝崩後，為永寧太僕，以名過其實，能用少也。正始中，遷侍中尚書僕射。豐在臺省，常多託疾，時臺制，疾滿百日當解祿，豐疾未滿數十日，輒暫起，已復臥，如是數歲。初，豐子韜以選尚公主，豐雖外辭之，內不甚憚也。豐弟翼及偉，仕數歲間，並歷郡守。豐嘗於人中顯誡二弟，言當用榮位為〔囗〕。及司馬宣王久病，偉為二千石，荒于酒，亂新平、扶風二郡而豐不召，眾人以為恃寵。曹爽專政，豐依違二公間，無有適莫，故于時有謗書曰：「曹爽之勢熱如湯，太傅父子冷如漿，李豐兄弟如游光。」其意以為豐雖外示清淨，而內圖事，有似於游光也。及宣王奏誅爽，住車闕下，與豐相聞，豐怖，遽氣索，足委地不能起。至嘉平四年宣王終後，中書令缺，大將軍諮問朝臣：「誰可補者？」或指向豐。豐雖知此非顯選，而自以連婚國家，思附至尊，因伏不辭，遂奏用之。豐為中書二歲，帝比每獨召與語，不知所說。景王知其議己，請豐，豐不以實告，乃殺之。其事祕。豐前後仕歷二朝，不以家計為意，仰俸廩而已。韜雖尚公主，豐常約敕不得有所侵取，時得賜錢帛，輒以外施親族；及得賜宮人，多與子弟，而豐皆以與諸外甥。及死後，有司籍其家，家無餘積。魏氏春秋曰：夜送豐尸付廷尉，廷尉鍾毓不受，曰：「非法官所治也。」以其狀告，且敕之，乃受。帝怒，將問豐死意，太后懼，呼帝入，乃止。遣使收翼。世語曰：翼後妻，散騎常侍荀廙姊，謂翼曰：「中書事發，可及書未至赴吳，何為坐取死亡！左右可共同赴水火者誰？」翼思未答，妻曰：「君在大州，不知可與同死生者，去亦不免。」翼曰：「二兒小，吾不去。今但從坐，身死，二兒必免。」果如翼言。翼子斌，楊駿外甥也。晉惠帝初，為河南尹，與駿俱死，見晉書。













[43] Shìyǔ states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán reached the Minister of Justice, would not agree to submit a statement. Minister of Justice Zhōng Yù personally oversaw the investigation of [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán with stern expression rebuked [Zhōng] Yù stating: “What statement should I make? You are a director-scribe for accusing people, you will make one for me.” [Zhōng] Yù believed that him a famed serviceman with integrity high that could not be bent, but the case needed its conclusion, in the night composed a statement, making it adhere with the situation, and shedding tears showed it to [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán looked and nodded at it and nothing more.130 [Zhōng] Yù’s younger brother [Zhōng] Huì was younger than [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Xiàhóu] Xuán had not associated with him. That day he was seated with [Zhōng] Yù and acted overly familiar toward [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Xiàhóu] Xuán would not accept.
Sūn Shèng’s Záyǔ states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán was in prison, [Zhōng] Huì took advantage to wish to be overly familiar with and befriend [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán with stern expression said: “Lord Zhōng why press me like this?”



〔四〕　世語曰：玄至廷尉，不肯下辭。廷尉鍾毓自臨治玄。玄正色責毓曰：「吾當何辭？卿為令史責人也，卿便為吾作。」毓以其名士，節高不可屈，而獄當竟，夜為作辭，令與事相附，流涕以示玄。玄視，頷之而已。毓弟會，年少於玄，玄不與交，是日於毓坐狎玄，玄不受。孫盛雜語曰：玄在囹圄，會因欲狎而友玄，玄正色曰：「鍾君何相偪如此也！」













[44] Wèi shū states: [Lǐ] Fēng’s son [Lǐ] Tāo due to being bestowed a princess was bestowed death inside the prison.



〔五〕　魏書曰：豐子韜，以尚主，賜死獄中。













[45] Wèilüè states: When [Xiàhóu] Xuán from the west returned, he did not interact in social affairs, and did not cultivate flowery ornamentation.
Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: Previously, Xiàhóu Bà was about to flee to Shǔ, called on [Xiàhóu] Xuán wishing to go with him. [Xiàhóu] Xuán said: “How can I uselessly cling to life by becoming a guest of enemy caitiffs?” Therefore he returned to the capital region. When the Grand Tutor [Sīmǎ Yì] died, Xǔ Yǔn spoke to [Xiàhóu] Xuán stating: “You have no further worries.” [Xiàhóu] Xuán sighed and said: “Shìzōng, how can you not see the situation? This man yet was able to deal with me as a younger man of a connected family, [Sīmǎ Shī] Zǐyuán and [Sīmǎ Zhāo] Zǐshàng cannot tolerate me.” [Xiàhóu] Xuán once wrote Discourses on Yuè Yì, Zhāng Liáng, and the Original Lack of Mutiliation Punishments, the statements and meanings profound and far-reaching, all transmitted through the world. When [Xiàhóu] Xuán was arrested, Guard General Sīmǎ [Zhāo] Wén-wáng shed tears and pleaded for him, the General-in-Chief [Sīmǎ Shī] said: “Have you forgotten the gathering at Excellency of Works Zhào’s burial?” Before this, Excellency of Works Zhào Yǎn had died, the General-in-Chief and his brothers gathered at the burial, the guests numbered in the hundreds. [Xiàhóu] Xuán arrived late, the multitude of guests all rose from their seats to greet him, the General-in-Chief because of this feared him.
Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: Cáo Shuǎng in Zhèngshǐ Fifth Year [244] attacked Shǔ, at the time [Xiàhóu] Xuán already was Overall Supervisor of Guānzhōng, reaching the Tenth Year [249], after [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed and exterminated, only then did he return to Luò. Citing Shào-dì jì, Excellency of Works Zhào Yǎn in the Sixth Year [245] died, [Xiàhóu] Xuán then had no way to attend [Zhào] Yǎn’s burial. If it is claimed that [Xiàhóu] Xuán attended Court, the annals and biographies also are without such a situation. This is probably not true.



〔六〕　魏略曰：玄自從西還，不交人事，不蓄華妍。魏氏春秋曰：初，夏侯霸將奔蜀，呼玄欲與之俱。玄曰：「吾豈苟存自客於寇虜乎？」遂還京師。太傅薨，許允謂玄曰：「無復憂矣。」玄歎曰：「士宗，卿何不見事乎？此人猶能以通家年少遇我，子元、子上不吾容也。」玄嘗著樂毅、張良及本無肉刑論，辭旨通遠，咸傳于世。玄之執也，衛將軍司馬文王流涕請之，大將軍曰：「卿忘會趙司空葬乎？」先是，司空趙儼薨，大將軍兄弟會葬，賓客以百數，玄時後至，眾賓客咸越席而迎，大將軍由是惡之。臣松之案：曹爽以正始五年伐蜀，時玄已為關中都督，至十年，爽誅滅後，方還洛耳。案少帝紀，司空趙儼以六年亡，玄則無由得會儼葬，若云玄入朝，紀、傳又無其事。斯近妄不實。






Xǔ Yǔn


Previously, Central Manager of the Army Gāoyáng’s Xǔ Yǔn with [Lǐ] Fēng and [Xiàhóu] Xuán was close and friendly. Before this there was a forged one-chǐ Edict letter, appointing [Xiàhóu] Xuán as General-in-Chief, [Xǔ] Yǔn as Grand Commandant, together overseeing Secretariat Writers affairs. There was an unknown person before dawn riding a horse with the Edict tablet, handed it to [Xǔ] Yǔn’s gate clerk, stating: “There is an Edict,” and then galloping away. [Xǔ] Yǔn at once threw the letter into a fire and burned it, not opening and presenting it to Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng. Later when the matter of [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest was discovered, transferred [Xǔ] Yǔn to Defending North General, Lent Stave as Overall Supervisor of Héběi’s varous military affairs. Before setting out, for giving out government property, arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice, exiled to Lèlàng, died on the road. [46]



初，中領軍高陽許允與豐、玄親善。先是有詐作尺一詔書，以玄為大將軍，允為太尉，共錄尚書事。有何人天未明乘馬以詔版付允門吏，曰「有詔」，因便馳走。允即投書燒之，不以開呈司馬景王。後豐等事覺，徙允為鎮北將軍，假節督河北諸軍事。未發，以放散官物，收付廷尉，徙樂浪，道死。〔一〕










[46] Wèilüè states: [Xǔ] Yǔn appellation Shìzōng was of a generationally powerful clan. His father [Xǔ] Jù served successively as Managing Agriculture Colonel and prefecture Administrator. [Xǔ] Yǔn as a youth with his same prefecture’s Cuī Zàn both were famed in Jì Province, summoned to enter the army. In Emperor Míng’s time became Secretariat Writers Selections Department Cadet, with Chén state’s Yuán Kǎn partnered, together implicated in an office affair, both arrested and sent to prison, the Edict’s intentions were strict and harsh, certain to have death penalties, with the upright one having heavier punishment. [Xǔ] Yǔn spoke with [Yuán] Kǎn stating: “You are an accomplished minister’s son, by law there should be the Eight Deliberations, you do not worry of death.” [Yuán] Kǎn understood his intention, and so accepted the heavier punishment. [Xǔ] Yǔn’s punishment completed and he was restored as a clerk, sent out as a prefecture Administrator, gradually promoted to Attendant Central Secretariat Writer Central Manager of the Army. [Xǔ] Yǔn heared that Lǐ Fēng and the rest had been arrested, wished to go see the General-in-Chief, had already exited the gates, turned and hesitated undecided, in the middle of the way returned to fetch scallions, [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest were already arrested completely. The General-in-Chief heard of [Xǔ] Yǔn’s previous hurry, was bewildered by it and said: “I myself arrested [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest, I don’t know why the scholar officials are rushing about.” At the time the Court councilors that were rushing were many, but everyone all knew he was thinking of [Xǔ] Yǔn. It happened that Defending North General Liú Jìng died, the Court appointed [Xǔ] Yǔn to succeed [Liú] Jìng. Having already received the Stave and Transfers, he went out to stay in an outer lodge. The General-in-Chief’s letter to [Xǔ] Yǔn said: “Although the Defending North has few affairs, yet it supervises and manages an entire region. I think of you beating flowery drums, establishing vermilion staves, through your home province, this is what is called ’Walking in daytime wearing embroidery.” [Xǔ] Yǔn in heart was extremely pleased, with the Terrace interior exchanged news, wishing to exchange his drums and trumpets and banners and flags. His elder brother’s son [Xǔ] Sù tended to hear of everyone saying that [Xǔ] Yǔn had previously met with suspicion, warned [Xǔ] Yǔn: “You should merely hurry off, what use is this?” [Xǔ] Yǔn said: “You are a common serviceman and do not understand, I am only glorifying the state, and therefore request this.” The Emperor because [Xǔ] Yǔn was about to depart thus had Edict to gather the various ministers, the various ministers all gathered, the Emperor specially summoned [Xǔ] Yǔn to come close. [Xǔ] Yǔn formerly had been an Attendant Central, considering he was about to be separated from the Emperor, he shed tears and sobbed. The gathering finished, ended and went out, Edict urged [Xǔ] Yǔn to quickly leave. It happened that relevant managers memorialized that [Xǔ] Yǔn had formerly without authority had kitchen cash and grain given to various performers and his office associates, therefore then arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice, the investigation and interrogation completed, spared death by exile to the borders. [Xǔ] Yǔn in Jiāpíng Sixth Year Autumn was exiled, his wife and children not permitted to accompany him, on the road and not yet arrived, in that year’s winter he died.
Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: [Xǔ] Yǔn became a Personnel Department Cadet, selecting prefecture Administrator. Emperor Míng suspected the employments were not in order, summoned him to enter, about to apply punishments. [Xǔ] Yǔn’s wife Ruǎn-shì barefooted went out, speaking stating: “An enlightened ruler can be persuaded by logic, difficult to be appealed by emotion.” [Xǔ] Yǔn nodded to her and then entered. The Emperor angrily interrogated him, [Xǔ] Yǔn replied stating: “Although this prefecture’s Administrator’s term limit document letter first arrived, the age limit was later. Although this other Administrator was later, the day limit was before.” The Emperor took the matters in front and looked at them, and then released and sent him out. Looking out and seeing his clothing was damaged, he said: “This is a pure clerk.” Bestowed on him. When [Xǔ] Yǔn was sent out as Defending North, he happily spoke with his wife stating: “I know I have escaped.” The wife said: “Disaster is seen in this, what escape is there?” [Xǔ] Yǔn excelled in appraising seals, when about to be appointed, because the seal was not good, he had it again recarved. It was like this three times. [Xǔ] Yǔn said: “Although the seal is just completed yet it is already disgraced.” Asked the seal deliverer, and indeed in carrying it had fallen in a lavatory.
Xiāng Yìn shū states: “The method of appraising seals originally came from Chén [Qún] Chángwén. Chángwén spoke of it to Wéi Zhòngjiāng, seal crafter Yáng Lì from Zhòngjiāng received the method, spoke of it to Xǔ Shìzōng. [Yáng] Lì with the method divined good and bad fortune, out of ten able to be correct nine to eight. Zhòngjiāng asked Chángwén ‘How did you obtain the method from?’ Chángwén said: ‘It originally came from the Hàn era. There were classics on appraising seals, appraising tablets, also there were classics on hawks, classics on oxen, classics on horses. Seal crafter Zōng Yǎng spoke of the method to Chéng Shēnbó, therefore there were twelve schools of appraisal methods transmitted to the world.’”
[Xǔ] Yǔn’s wife Ruǎn-shì was worthy and enlightened but ugly, [Xǔ] Yǔn on first seeing her was amazed, after the marriage rituals finished, he had no intention to enter (her room) again. The wife sent a maidservant to spy on him, saying: “There is a guest surnamed Huán.” The wife said: “It must be Huán Fàn, he will urge him to enter.” Soon after [Huán] Fàn indeed urged him, [Xǔ] Yǔn entered, and immediately then rose, the wife clutched his garment to detain him. [Xǔ] Yǔn looked back and spoke to the wife stating: “Women have Four Virtues, how many do you have?” The wife said: “Your new wife lacks only appearance. Servicemen have a Hundred Conducts, how many do you have?” Xǔ said: “All of them.” The wife said: “Servicemen have a Hundred Conducts, taking virtue as foremost. You love beauty and do not love virtue, how can you say all of them?” [Xǔ] Yǔn had a shamed expression, knew she was out of the ordinary, and therefore they became close and respected one another. Begat two sons, [Xǔ] Qí and [Xǔ] Měng, from youth had good reputation. [Xǔ] Yǔn later was executed by [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng, his disciple ran to enter to inform his wife, the wife just was at her loom, her expression did not change, and said: “I already knew it would be like this.” The disciple wished to hide the children, the wife said: “Do not pre-empt the affairs of the boys.” Later they moved to where the grave was, [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng sent Zhōng Huì to watch them, and if their talents and skills and virtues and abilities reached their father’s, then arrest them. The boys spoke of this to their mother, their mother answered: “Although you are fine, your talents and capabilities are not many, speak with [Zhōng] Huì from the heart, then you will assuredly be without worries. Do not show utmost grief, when [Zhōng] Huì stops then you stop. Also you can somewhat ask about Court affairs.” The boys followed this. [Zhōng] Huì returned from the mission, reported the situation, in the end they escaped from disaster, all by their mother’s instructions. Even with [Zhōng] Huì’s knowledge and discernment, yet he was beaten by the wisdom of a worthy wife; indeed celebrations reached to later successors, bequeathing fiefs to descendants and nothing more.
Shìyǔ states: [Xǔn] Yǔn’s two sons, [Xǔ] Qí appellation Zǐtài, [Xǔ] Měng appellation Zǐbào, both had administration talent and scholarship. During Jìn’s Yuánkāng [291 - 299], [Xǔ] Qí was Director of Retainers Colonel, [Xǔ] Měng was Yōu Province Inspector.
Fù Chàng’s Jìn Zhūgōng zàn states: [Xǔ] Měng in ritual and music was scholarly and refined, at the time the most exceptional. [Xǔ] Qí’s son [Xǔ] Xiá appellation Sīzǔ, for purity and esteem was acclaimed, position reached Attendant Central. [Xǔ] Měng’s son [Xǔ] Shì appellation Yízǔ, had talent and competence, reached Púyáng Inner Scribe, Píngyuán Administrator.



〔一〕　魏略曰：允字士宗，世冠族。父據，仕歷典農校尉、郡守。允少與同郡崔贊俱發名於冀州，召入軍。明帝時為尚書選曹郎，與陳國袁侃對，同坐職事，皆收送獄，詔旨嚴切，當有死者，正直者為重。允謂侃曰：「卿，功臣之子，法應八議，不憂死也。」侃知其指，乃為受重。允刑竟復吏，出為郡守，稍遷為侍中尚書中領軍。允聞李豐等被收，欲往見大將軍，已出門，回遑不定，中道還取蔥，豐等已收訖。大將軍聞允前遽，怪之曰：「我自收豐等，不知士大夫何為匆匆乎？」是時朝臣遽者多耳，而眾人咸以為意在允也。會鎮北將軍劉靜卒，朝廷以允代靜。已受節傳，出止外舍。大將軍與允書曰：「鎮北雖少事，而都典一方，念足下震華鼓，建朱節，歷本州，此所謂著繡晝行也。」允心甚悅，與臺中相聞，欲易其鼓吹旌旗。其兄子素頗聞眾人說允前見嫌意，戒允「但當趣耳，用是為邪」！允曰：「卿俗士不解，我以榮國耳，故求之。」帝以允當出，乃詔會群臣，群臣皆集，帝特引允以自近；允前為侍中，顧當與帝別，涕泣歔欷。會訖，罷出，詔促允令去。會有司奏允前擅以廚錢穀乞諸俳及其官屬，故遂收送廷尉，考問竟，（故）減死徙邊。允以嘉平六年秋徙，妻子不得自隨，行道未到，以其年冬死。魏氏春秋曰：允為吏部郎，選郡守。明帝疑其所用非次，召入，將加罪。允妻阮氏跣出，謂曰：「明主可以理奪，難以情求。」允頷之而入。帝怒詰之，允對曰：「某郡太守雖限滿文書先至，年限在後，〔某守雖後〕，日限在前。」帝前取事視之，乃釋遣出。望其衣敗，曰：「清吏也。」賜之。允之出為鎮北也，喜謂其妻曰：「吾知免矣！」妻曰：「禍見於此，何免之有？」允善相印，將拜，以印不善，使更刻之，如此者三。允曰：「印雖始成而已被辱。」問送印者，果懷之而墜于廁。相印書曰：「相印法本出陳長文，長文以語韋仲將，印工楊利從仲將受法，以語許士宗。利以法術占吉凶，十可中八九。仲將問長文『從誰得法』？長文曰：『本出漢世，有相印、相笏經，又有鷹經、牛經、馬經。印工宗養以法語程申伯，是故有一十二家相法傳于世。』」允妻阮氏賢明而醜，允始見愕然，交禮畢，無復入意。妻遣婢覘之，云「有客姓桓」，妻曰：「是必桓範，將勸使入也。」既而範果勸之。允入，須臾便起，妻捉裾留之。允顧謂婦曰：「婦有四德，卿有其幾？」婦曰：「新婦所乏唯容。士有百行，君有其幾？」許曰：「皆備。」婦曰：「士有百行，以德為首，君好色不好德，何謂皆備？」允有慚色，知其非凡，遂雅相親重。生二子，奇、猛，少有令聞。允後為景王所誅，門生走入告其婦，婦正在機，神色不變，曰：「早知爾耳。」門生欲藏其子，婦曰：「無預諸兒事。」後移居墓所，景王遣鍾會看之，若才藝德能及父，當收。兒以語母，母答：「汝等雖佳，才具不多，率胸懷與會語，便自無憂，不須極哀，會止便止。又可多少問朝事。」兒從之。會反命，具以狀對，卒免其禍，皆母之教也。雖會之識鑒，而輸賢婦之智也。果慶及後嗣，追封子孫而已。世語曰：允二子：奇字子泰，猛字子豹，並有治理才學。晉元康中，奇為司隸校尉，猛幽州刺史。傅暢晉諸公贊曰：猛禮樂儒雅，當時最優。奇子遐，字思祖，以清尚稱，位至侍中。猛子式，字儀祖，有才幹，至濮陽內史、平原太守。







Wáng Jīng


Qīnghé’s Wáng Jīng also with [Xǔ] Yǔn both were acclaimed as Jì Province’s famed servicemen. During Gānlù [256 - 260] he became a Secretariat Writer, in connection to the Duke of Gāoguì village incident was executed. At first when [Wáng] Jīng became a prefecture Administrator, [Wáng] Jīng’s mother spoke to [Wáng] Jīng stating: “You are a farming family’s son, now your service reaches the two thousand dàn. Things going too far is inauspicious, you can stop.” [Wáng] Jīng did not follow this, successively was Inspector in two provinces, Director of Retainers Colonel, in the end bringing about destruction. [47] [Xǔ] Yǔn’s friend of the same prefecture Cuī Zàn, also had once warned [Xǔ] Yǔn of flourishing too much in the world. [48]



清河王經亦與允俱稱冀州名士。甘露中為尚書，坐高貴鄉公事誅。始經為郡守，經母謂經曰：「汝田家子，今仕至二千石，物太過不祥，可以止矣。」經不能從，歷二州刺史，司隸校尉，終以致敗〔一〕。允友人同郡崔贊，亦嘗以處世太盛戒允云。〔二〕










[47] Shìyǔ states: [Wáng] Jīng appellation Yànwěi, previously was Jiāngxià Administrator. General-in-Chief Cáo Shuǎng sent silk fabric of twenty pǐ to trade with Wú, [Wáng] Jīng did not send the letter, abandoned office and returned home. His mother asked the circumstances of his return, [Wáng] Jīng replied with the truth. His mother believed [Wáng] Jīng managed troops and horses but without authority left, and in answer had the escort clerks cane [Wáng] Jīng fifty strokes, [Cáo] Shuǎng heard and did not further punish him. [Wáng] Jīng became Director of Retainers Colonel, recruited Hénèi’s Xiàng Xióng as Overall Office Following Official. When Wáng Yè went out, he did not explain [Wáng] Jīng’s intentions, so that it reached trouble. When [Wáng] Jīng was executed in the East Market, [Xiàng] Xióng wept for him, emotionally moving the entire market. The execution reached to [Wáng] Jīng’s mother, Yōng Province former clerk Huángfǔ Yàn with his family wealth collected and buried her.
Hàn Jìn Chūnqiū states: When [Wáng] Jīng was arrested, he took leave of his mother. His mother’s expression did not change, laughed and answered stating: “Of people who does not die? Formerly the reason that I did not stop you was that I feared you would not find your place. To like this share fate, what regret is to be had?” Jìn Emperor Wǔ’s Tàishǐ Inaugural Year [265] Edict stated: “Former Secretariat Writer Wáng Jīng, although personally entrapped in penal law, however his maintaining of will can be praised. The household is fallen and lost, my thoughts always pity this, thus bestow on [Wáng] Jīng’s grandson Cadet Central position.”



〔一〕　世語曰：經字（彥偉）〔彥緯〕，初為江夏太守。大將軍曹爽附絹二十匹令交市于吳，經不發書，棄官歸。母問歸狀，經以實對。母以經典兵馬而擅去，對送吏杖經五十，爽聞，不復罪。經為司隸校尉，辟河內向雄為都官從事，王業之出，不申經（竟）〔意〕以及難。經刑於東市，雄哭之，感動一市。刑及經母，雍州故吏皇甫晏以家財收葬焉。漢晉春秋曰：經被收，辭母。母顏色不變，笑而應曰：「人誰不死？往所以不止汝者，恐不得其所也。以此并命，何恨之有哉？」晉武帝太始元年詔曰：「故尚書王經，雖身陷法辟，然守志可嘉。門戶堙沒，意常愍之，其賜經孫郎中。」













[48] Xún Chuò’s Jìzhōu jì states: [Cuī] Zàn’s son [Cuī] Hóng appellation Liángbó, was pure and scrupulous and had determination to act not for himself, became a Jìn Personnel Department Secretariat Writer, Minister of Agriculture.



〔二〕　荀綽冀州記曰：贊子洪，字良伯，清恪有匪躬之志，為晉吏部尚書、大司農。
crumbs: 9  Biographies of the various Xiàhóu and Cáo

title: 9  Biographies of the various Xiàhóu and Cáo
text:
Appraisal


Appraisal states: The Xiàhóu and Cáo clans for generations intermarried, therefore [Xiàhóu] Dūn, [Xiàhóu] Yuān, [Cáo] Rén, [Cáo] Hóng, [Cáo] Xiū, [Xiàhóu] Shàng, [Cáo] Zhēn and others all as kin and old relations of lungs and guts, were noble and valued at the time, Left and Right of the achievements and enterprise, all having effective labors. [Cáo] Shuǎng’s virtue was meager but position honored, submerging into overflowing, this assuredly is what the Dà Yì wrote of, what the Dào school dreaded. [Xiàhóu] Xuán for his standards and bearing, the world praised his name, however he and Cáo Shuǎng inside and outside were inseparably entangled, with glorious position like this, one never hears of rectifying or correcting in (Cáo Shuǎng’s) wrongs, or assisting in delivering good talents. Raising this for discussion, how could he have escaped this?



評曰：夏侯、曹氏，世為婚姻，故惇、淵、仁、洪、休、尚、真等並以親舊肺腑，貴重于時，左右勳業，咸有效勞。爽德薄位尊，沈溺盈溢，此固大易所著，道家所忌也。玄以規格局度，世稱其名，然與曹爽中外繾綣；榮位如斯，曾未聞匡弼其非，援致良才。舉茲以論，焉能免之乎！
crumbs: 9  Biographies of the various Xiàhóu and Cáo

title: 9  Biographies of the various Xiàhóu and Cáo
text:
Xiàhóu Yīng was an early follower of Liú Bāng, founder of Former Hàn.↩︎
Major (sīmǎ) was a chief of staff for military affairs.↩︎
This appointment is perhaps notable in that this was Cáo Cāo’s previous position before becoming Yǎn Province Governor.↩︎
Bowed head (kòutóu) is to bow to press the forehead to the ground. The term is the source of the loan word “kowtow.”↩︎
Another interpretation of “severely rebuked” (shù zé) is “counted and rebuked” or “numbered and rebuked,” as in to list out all the charges and accusations against a criminal.↩︎
Guāng-Wǔ jì is an annals of Later Hàn Emperor Guāng-Wǔ. However, this story does not appear in the now canonical annals of Guāng-Wǔ in Fàn Yè’s Hòu Hàn shū 1, so Sūn Shèng is using a different history of Later Hàn. Fàn Yè’s Hòu Hàn shū instead has the story in Hòu Hàn shū 10.↩︎
Noble Lady (guìrén) was a rank in a harem. The term mǔ dì can also mean “younger brother of the same mother,” but the account in Hòu Hàn shū 10 clarifies that both lady Yīn’s mother and younger brother were taken hostage.↩︎
In this context combined strike (hé jī) probably refers to attacking both hostages and hostage takers.↩︎
Emperor Ān of Hàn (r. 106 - 125) and Emperor Shùn of Hàn (r. 125 - 144).↩︎
From this context it is clear that Xiàhóu Dūn’s eye wound occurred during the campaigns against Lǚ Bù in 194. However, the canonical annotations to the biography of Lǚ Bù in Hòu Hàn shū 75 cite this passage as part of a broader summary of Xiàhóu Dūn’s career in connection to Xiàhóu Dūn being mentioned as participating of the campaign against Lǚ Bù in 198. This creates a false impression that Xiàhóu Dūn’s eye wound occurred in the 198 campaign, and is probably the source for the incorrect myth that Xiàhóu Dūn’s eye wound occurred in 198 perpetuated by Sān Guó Yǎnyì and other nonhistorical sources.↩︎
This appointment is perhaps notable in that Zhāng Miǎo had been Administrator of Chénliú, meaning that Xiàhóu Dūn was probably being entrusted to pacify the region that had been the heart of the rebellion against Cáo Cāo.↩︎
This appointment is perhaps notable in that Hénán Intendant held censorial authority over central government positions. It is possible this appointment occurred around the same time that Cáo Cāo was appointed Director of Retainers Colonel, which also held censorial authority. Under normal administration, Hénán Intendant was the head of Hénán prefecture, which contained the capital city of Luòyáng, while Director of Retainers Colonel was the head of Sīlì, the province containing the capital city of Luòyáng.↩︎
Subduing Waves General (fúbō jiāngjūn) was a Miscellaneous Title General that had been famously used for Lù Bódé during Former Hàn and for Mǎ Yuán during Later Hàn. It had more recently been used again for Chén Dēng. Xiàhóu Dūn’s appointment probably was to succeed Chén Dēng, which a limit on Chén Dēng’s death as occuring sometime before or during 204, as Chén Dēng’s death year is not otherwise known.↩︎
From context, the reward of musicians and singers was to commemorate the achievement of Sūn Quán’s formal surrender to have Xiàhóu Dūn’s Jūcháo garrison removed. It was not a bestowal of “prostitues and female entertainers” as claimed by Lu Yimin in the utterly ridiculous PhD thesis “Talons and Fangs of the Eastern Han Warlords.”↩︎
When Cáo Cāo became Duke of Wèi and later King of Wèi, Wèi officials formally became his subjects and would have to observe certain rituals of being servants to Cáo Cāo. Xiàhóu Dūn was being specially honored to not be a servant of Cáo Cāo and instead remain Cáo Cāo’s peer with both of them being Hàn officials.↩︎
Reconsideration here is sān sī, literally “three times thinking.”↩︎
It is also possible that the word here is the personal name Shào, as in ”select Dūn’s close relative [Xiàhóu] Shào and enfeoff him,” but this interpretation is uncertain as there is no other record of a Xiàhóu Shào.↩︎
the term sūn yì literally means “decreases and increases,” referring to what policies to abandon or adopt.↩︎
The term zú dì usually refers to a younger third cousin of the same male-line clan. First or second cousins of the same male-line clan are cóng dì.↩︎
Xiàhóu Yuān may have been succeeding Shǐ Huàn, who is noted to have died in that year.↩︎
Yúmí and Qiān counties were in Yòufúfēng. The Dī were a foreign tribal people to the west.↩︎
Hù county was in Yòufúfēng.↩︎
Jì county was in Hànyáng/Tiānshuǐ prefecture.↩︎
Lǔchéng was in Yànmén prefecture↩︎
Qíshān was in Hànyáng/Tiānshuǐ prefecture, near Xī county.↩︎
Xiǎnqīn county was in Hànyáng/Tiānshuǐ prefecture.↩︎
Lüèyáng county was in Hànyáng/Tiānshuǐ prefecture.↩︎
Xīngguó was in Lüèyáng county.↩︎
Chánglí was in Lüèyáng county.↩︎
Gāopíng county was in Āndìng prefecture.↩︎
The Stave (jié) granted authority to act as an Imperial agent, only submitting a report after acting. The qualifier Lent (jiǎ) was due to the authority being temporary and revocable.↩︎
Hěshǒu “head of the Hé” refers to the source of the Huáng Hé, or Yellow River. The term Pacifying Hàn (Píng Hàn) can also be understood as “Equal to Hàn,” though this interpretation seems less likely.↩︎
Fūhǎn county was in Lǒngxī prefecture.↩︎
Héguān county was in Lǒngxī prefecture.↩︎
Xiǎohuángzhōng was on the border between Xīpíng and Jīnchéng prefectures.↩︎
Héxī refers generically to the area west of the upper courses of the Hé/Yellow River, Lǒngyòu refers generically to the areas west of Lǒng mountain. The territory of Liáng province was sometimes informally classified into these two subdivisions.↩︎
This is a reference to Lúnyǔ 5.9.↩︎
Xiàbiàn county was in Wǔdū prefecture.↩︎
Xiūtíng or Xiū precinct was in Qiān county in Yòufúfēng.↩︎
Abatis (lùjiǎo), literally “deer horns,” were a field defense made from cut down trees with sharpened branches and wood facing the enemy.↩︎
Fèi and Huá counties were in Tàishān in Yǎn Province; Táo Qiān had previously invaded and captured these counties. Jìmó county was in Běihǎi prefecture in Qīng Province, Kǎiyáng county was in Lángyé prefecture in Xú Province.↩︎
Gōuyáng county was in Jǐyīn prefecture.↩︎
Yǐnqiáng county was in Rǔnán prefecture.↩︎
Jīluò mountain was in Mì county in Hénán.↩︎
The term huīxià, literally “below the signal flag,” referred to an officer’s personal direct command.↩︎
Yuān county was in Nányáng prefecture. The character is also pronounced Wǎn, but the reading Yuān is preferred here to avoid confusion with Wǎn county in Lújiāng prefecture.↩︎
Yānlíng county was in Yǐngchuān prefecture.↩︎
Chén county was in Chén state.↩︎
Línyǐng county was in Yǐngchuān prefecture.↩︎
Nínglíng county was in Liáng prefecture.↩︎
Mèng Bēn and Xià Yù were legendary warriors from the Warring States era.↩︎
Lóngkàng county was in Pèi prefecture.↩︎
Dōng’ē was in Dōng prefecture. Jǐyīn and Shānyáng were prefectures, and in this context refer to the counties containing the prefectural capitals. Zhōngmù, Yángwǔ, Jīng, Mì counties were in Hénán prefecture.↩︎
Wǔyáng was in Yǐngchuān, Yīn, Shè, Dǔyáng, Bówàng were in Nányáng. The name of Shè county is sometimes also given as Yè, as in modern times the pronunciation Yè is more common for the character.↩︎
Yěwáng county was in Hénèi prefecture.↩︎
Dūyáng county was in Dōnghǎi prefecture.↩︎
Qíchūn county was in Jiāngxià prefecture.↩︎
Xiàbiàn county was in Wǔdū prefecture.↩︎
Gùshān or Gù mountain was probably in or near Dīdào county in Wǔdū prefecture.↩︎
Chariot Carriage (chējià) refers to the Emperor’s chariot and by extension to the Emperor himself. Superior (shàng) is a third person term for the Emperor. The timing of this event is slightly uncertain as there were a few months between the death of Xiàhóu Dūn and the actual ascension of Cáo Pī as Emperor, so there is a possibility that these Imperial terms are being used anachronstically.↩︎
Lìyáng county was in Jiǔjiāng/Huáinán prefecture.↩︎
Wúhú county was in Dānyáng prefecture.↩︎
Dòngpǔ was in Lìyáng county.↩︎
Chángpíng county was in Chén state.↩︎
Wǎn county was in Lújiāng prefecture.↩︎
Xúnyáng county was in Lújiāng prefecture.↩︎
Where (the Emperor) was traveling (xíng zài suǒ) was a term for where the Emperor happened to be, often used for when the Emperor was not at the Palace.↩︎
Língqiū county was in Dài prefecture.↩︎
Niúzhū was in Dānyáng county.↩︎
Shàolíng county was in Rǔnán prefecture.↩︎
The personal name of an individual’s father would usually be a name taboo for the individual in most situations. It would be very awkward for someone to be given a fief sharing a character with their father’s personal name.↩︎
Méi county was in Yòufúfēng.↩︎
The character for Yé is also pronounced Xié, which is favored in modern times, though Yé is believed closer to the ancient pronunciation.↩︎
Shūxiàng was a Spring and Autumn era Jìn state man who cared for the orphans of a decease colleague.↩︎
Píng was the posthumous name of Yàn Yīng, a Spring and Autumn era Qí state man. He reportedly took care to maintain steadfast loyalty to lifetime friends through changing fortunes.↩︎
Fèi fǔ yí xù, literally ”legacy thread of lungs and bowels.”↩︎
Gāoyáng is a song in the Shījīng. The relevant phrase ”from the public” (zì gōng) is a term for frugality, deriving from a lyric of an official leaving Court to return home to eat his own private food rather than eat from public resources.↩︎
The term here is qí ài. Qí is a term for someone in their sixties, Ài in their fifties.↩︎
This phrase kè míng kè lèi is from the song Huáng Yǐ in the Shījīng.↩︎
This account creates a problem in that Sīmǎ Xuān-wáng is Sīmǎ Yì, who did not participate in the campaign and therefore could not have spoken to Xiàhóu Xuán. Zīzhì Tōngjiàn attempts to resolve the discrepancy by changing this account to a letter rather than a conversation. Jìn shū instead claims that Sīmǎ Xuān-wáng should be Sīmǎ Wén-wáng, or Sīmǎ Zhāo, who did accompany the campaign as Xiàhóu Xuán’s second in command.↩︎
Zīzhì Tōngjiàn somewhat rewrites the account given here to delete “the mobilize oxen and horses,” which has probably led to the popular belief that the west of the passes was depopulated of people.↩︎
Tāngmù was land used for revenue for fiefs within the royal domain, particularly for fiefs for in-laws and princesses.↩︎
The term rendered as “harsh words” is shēn wén, which is to use an excessively harsh and distorted interpretation of written law for entrapment.↩︎
“Creation of power” (zuō wēi) is a term referring to the monarch’s authority to order punishments and executions.↩︎
Chariot Carriage (chéngyú) originally was one of the Emperor’s chariots and became a euphemism for the Emperor’s person.↩︎
Secretariat Crafters (shàngfāng) were master artisans employed by the Imperial Palace to craft objects for the Imperial family.↩︎
Talent Ladies (cáirén) were a rank in the Imperial harem. Based on the name presumably they were employed for various skills and arts.↩︎
The exact term used here is Jiéyú, a rank in the Imperial harem↩︎
The term translated as “fascicle” here is piān, which refers to a set of bamboo writing strips bound together into a rollable bundle.↩︎
The source citation for this annotation seems to have been lost, unfortunately.↩︎
“Home province” here is běnzhōu, which can sound close to “Bìng Province” bìngzhōu.↩︎
Two Palaces refer to the Emperor and the Dowager Empress. Bone and flesh refer to biological family relationships. Its use here is probably a rather crude propaganda, as the Emperor Cáo Fāng was not an actual biological, or ”bone and flesh,” son of the Dowager Empress.↩︎
The translation as ”past” is from interpreting wǎng 枉 as an equivalent variant of (or an error for) wǎng 往.↩︎
Zhào Gāo was the overly powerful Chancellor during the downfall of Qín, who dominated the government to the point that he was able to arrange for the death of the Qín Second Emperor. The incorrect popular belief that Zhào Gāo was a eunuch seems to derive from a Táng dynasty era misunderstanding.↩︎
The Lǚ clan dominated the Hàn government through the Dowager Empress Lǚ after the death of Hàn Emperor Gāo, but was overthrown and exterminated soon after the Dowager’s death. The Huò clan dominated Hàn through the powerful regent Huò Guāng after the death of Hàn Emperor Wǔ, but was overthrown and exterminated soon after Huò Guāng’s death.↩︎
Yǒngníng Palace was the Palace of the Dowager Empress.↩︎
The Grand Kitchen (tàiguān) was responsible for the Emperor’s food and meals.↩︎
Extermination of the Three Clans (sān zú) was a mass execution of the criminal’s family members as organized into three groups, generally reserved for cases of state treason. The definition of the Three Clans has varied between texts and times. Example definitions include: “father and mother, elder and younger brothers, wife and children;” “father’s clan, mother’s clan, wife’s clan,” and “father and his brothers, self and his brothers, son and his brothers.” Qín had previously also defined a “Five Clans” and “Seven Clans,” and from Suí onward there was a “Nine Clans.”↩︎
The term yá chái 崖柴 is a variant form of ái chái 啀喍, which refers to a dog opening its mouth and baring its fangs threateningly.↩︎
The term túsū (Japanese pronunciation toso) is now more commonly used for a medicinal liquor served on the new year. The name is believed to have derived fron the name of an herb, and some building complexes would have a structure decorated with pictures of the túsū herb, and therefore be called túsū.↩︎
Zhòngcháng is a two-character family name.↩︎
This was a critical role in the coup: Central Manager of the Army was the position held by Cáo Shuǎng’s own brother Cáo Xī.↩︎
In ancient time keeping, the day was divided into twelve two-hour blocks. Of these, the fifth watch (wǔ gǔ) corresponds to the modern 3:00-5:00 AM.↩︎
Língtái was the name of a terrace, often used for astronomical observation and astrology.↩︎
This is a reference to a story preserved in the Zuǒ Zhuàn Duke Āi Seventh Year. Someone in Cáo state dreamed of spirits gathering to plan the destruction of Cáo state. The spirit of Shūzhènduó, the founder of Cáo state, pleaded to wait until a Gōngsūn Qiáng came to power. Later, a commoner named Gōngsūn Qiáng indeed came to power and Cáo state was indeed conquered and destroyed.↩︎
Shūzhènduó was the founder of Cáo state. In the story of the man dreaming of Cáo state’s destruction, the spirit of Shūzhènduó pleaded on Cáo state’s behalf.↩︎
When Hàn Emperor Ān died suddenly, his widow the Empress Yán and her brother Yán Xiǎn came to power as regents over a hastily enthroned child Emperor. When their child puppet suddenly died of illness, a group of nineteen eunuchs took advantage of the opening to launch a coup, killing Yán Xiǎn.↩︎
The word here is guàn 灌 ”to irrigate, to pour” and is probably being used as a variant of jiāng 韁 ”reins, bridle.”↩︎
The East Market was the location of public executions.↩︎
Lǎo-zǐ was a Spring and Autumn era thinker, Zhuāng-zǐ a Warring States era thinker. Their work became the foundation for what is now called “Dào-ism” (Wade-Giles: Taoism).↩︎
“Discourse (lùn) on Way (dào) and Virtue (dé)”↩︎
Redundant officials (rǒng guān) were government officials without designated regular duties or tasks, used for ad hoc tasks.↩︎
This scandalous accusation is probably false. See Péi Sōngzhī’s comment below.↩︎
The biography of Féi Yī in SGZ 44 includes an annotation stating that Hé Yàn’s son was indeed killed. If Wèi Mò zhuàn is not incorrect here, it is possible that “pardoned and did not kill” refers to Hé Yàn’s wife (the King of Pèi’s sister), not Hé Yàn’s son.↩︎
The quotes are from the Xì Cí commentary in the Yìjīng, describing the aspects of a sage.↩︎
The term for “gentry” here is jìn shēn, literally “inserted through the sash,” referring to how gentry officials would have ceremonial tablets inserted and tucked into their belt sashes.↩︎
Note that the Lady Dù was the mother of Qín Lǎng, the other famous stepson adopted by Cáo Cāo. Probably Wèi Mò zhuàn confused the mothers of Hé Yàn and Qín Lǎng.↩︎
According to Hú Sānxǐng’s commentary in the Zīzhì Tōngjiàn, oiled ships were boats coated with a layer of oil to repel water.↩︎
Though this biography dates Xiàhóu Shàng’s illness as starting in the Sixth Year, the Treatises on Astronomy in Jìn shū record that Xiàhóu Shàng did not actually die until the Fourth Moon of the Seventh Year (226).↩︎
Friends in plain clothes (bùyī zhī jiāo) refers to a friendship formed before achieving high rank and status.↩︎
Bone and flesh (gǔ ròu) is an idiom for biological relation, and can perhaps be considered an equivalent for the English ”flesh and blood.”↩︎
Capping (ruò guàn) referred to the ceremony marking the transition to adulthood, when a man began wearing an adult headdress and hat. The ceremony was usually performed at age twenty in traditional reckoning.↩︎
Ivory Gates (yámén) referred to the office tents of Generals, which were marked by ivory-tipped banners to form gates.↩︎
The qín and sè are two ancient stringed instruments, celebrated for being able to harmonize with one another. To have the two play the same note is a waste of their ability to harmonize different notes.↩︎
Yī Yǐn was a celebrated minsiter of the Yīn dynasty. Zhōu-gōng was a celebrated minister of the Zhōu dynasty. The ruling family of Zhōu had the surname Jī.↩︎
This refers to the Emperor personally attending the ceremony, and soldiers posted at the ramp steps at the various gates of the Palace complex.↩︎
The pepper rooms (jiāo fáng) referred to the households of the Empress. The name referred to a Hàn dynasty era Palace of that name, referring to the use of a pepper paint for its fragrance.↩︎
Pǐ is a unit of silk.↩︎
Wandering lights (yóu guāng) is a name for a number of different legends and myths. Likely the one referred here is a ghostly light, similar to the will-o’-wisp.↩︎
The conviction of Xiàhóu Xuán was already pre-determined. Xiàhóu Xuán refused to participate in the farce and therefore refused to make a statement. Zhōng Yù therefore was obligated to compose a confession for Xiàhóu Xuán, making the confession adhere to the needs of the conviction.↩︎
